源码文档：A component for [restitution], controlling how bouncy a [rigid body] or [collider] is.

The coefficient should be between 0 and 1, where 0 corresponds to a **perfectly inelastic** collision with zero bounce,
and 1 corresponds to a **perfectly elastic** collision that tries to preserve all kinetic energy.
Values larger than 1 can result in unstable or explosive behavior.

If a collider does not have [`Restitution`] specified, the [`Restitution`] of its rigid body entity will be used instead.
If that is not specified either, collisions use the [`DefaultRestitution`] resource. The default restitution is set to 0,
meaning that objects are not bouncy by default.

[restitution]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coefficient_of_restitution
[rigid body]: crate::dynamics::RigidBody
[collider]: crate::dynamics::Collider

# Combine Rule

When two bodies collide, their coefficients are combined using the specified [`CoefficientCombine`] rule.
In the case of clashing rules, the following priority order is used: `Max > Multiply > Min > GeometricMean > Average`.

By default, restitution uses [`CoefficientCombine::Average`], computing the average `(a + b) / 2.0`.

# Usage

Create a new [`Restitution`] component with a restitution coefficient of `0.4`:

```ignore
Restitution::new(0.4)
```

Configure how two restitution coefficients are combined with [`CoefficientCombine`]:

```ignore
Restitution::new(0.4).with_combine_rule(CoefficientCombine::Max)
```

Combine the properties of two [`Restitution`] components:

```
#
let first = Restitution::new(0.8).with_combine_rule(CoefficientCombine::Average);
let second = Restitution::new(0.5).with_combine_rule(CoefficientCombine::Multiply);

// `CoefficientCombine::Multiply` has higher priority, so the coefficients are multiplied
assert_eq!(
    first.combine(second),
    Restitution::new(0.4).with_combine_rule(CoefficientCombine::Multiply)
);
```

# Accuracy

Restitution is not guaranteed to be entirely accurate, especially for fast-moving bodies
or when there are multiple contact points.

- Even with a coefficient of 1, some kinetic energy can be lost over long periods of time for bouncing objects.
  This can be caused by [friction](Friction), [damping](crate::dynamics::LinearDamping), or simulation inaccuracies.

- Collisions can have more or less bounce than expected, especially when objects are moving very fast.
  This is largely due to the the sequential solver and [continuous collision](crate::dynamics::ccd) scheme.

- An object falling flat on the ground with multiple contact points may tip over on one side or corner a bit.
  This is because contact points are solved sequentially, and the order of contact points affects the result.
  Configuring [`SolverConfig::restitution_iterations`](crate::dynamics::solver::SolverConfig::restitution_iterations)
  may help mitigate this.

- When collision velocity is small, collisions are treated as inelastic to prevent jitter. The velocity threshold can be
  configured using [`SolverConfig::restitution_threshold`](crate::dynamics::solver::SolverConfig::restitution_threshold).

For game purposes however, restitution should still be reasonably accurate.

It is worth noting that in real life, restitution coefficients can vary greatly based on material combinations
and numerous other factors, and they are not uniform across surfaces. For game purposes however, it is impractical to consider
all of these factors, so instead, material interactions are controlled using simple [`CoefficientCombine`] rules.

源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

[`MessageReader`]: super::MessageReader
[`MessageWriter`]: super::MessageWriter
[`message_update_system`]: super::message_update_system

源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

[`MessageReader`]: super::MessageReader
[`MessageWriter`]: super::MessageWriter
[`message_update_system`]: super::message_update_system

源码文档：Whether or not an entity is visible in the hierarchy.

This is a computed component that users should not change manually.
To set the visibility of an entity, use [`Visibility`] instead.
For more information, see [module level documentation](self#what-is-the-difference-between-visibility-components).

This property is updated in [`VisibilityPropagate`] in the [`PostUpdate`] schedule.
Until then, it is not up to date with [`Visibility`] if it was changed
in the same frame.

If this is false, then [`ViewVisibility`] should also be false.

[`VisibilityPropagate`]: VisibilitySystems::VisibilityPropagate

bevy_ui_render::extract_text_decorations：按文字段的布局几何与颜色，为变化的可见文字生成背景矩形及两类装饰线，装饰色可覆盖文字色；结合可编辑文字滚动偏移和裁剪，将各绘制项加入对应相机和层次。 参数范围：主世界；只读声明。
bevy_ui_render::extract_text_shadows：为变化的可见文字按 TextShadow 偏移、颜色和节点缩放生成字形阴影，按文本段及图集分组，并为删除线和下划线生成同色阴影；沿用编辑滚动位置和文字裁剪。 参数范围：主世界；只读声明。
bevy_ui_render::extract_text_sections：对变化的可见文字，按文本段取得颜色并生成字形位置及图集矩形，彩色字形保留白色乘色，选中字形可用光标样式覆盖颜色；应用编辑滚动和裁剪，并按连续图集分组为渲染节点。 参数范围：主世界；只读声明。
bevy_ui_render::text::extract_text_cursor：对变化的可见文字，按焦点及读写模式选择选区颜色，调整相邻行交接处的选区圆角，并依据光标可见状态生成光标矩形；静态文字不生成选区或光标，保留编辑滚动和裁剪。 参数范围：主世界；只读声明。
bevy_ui_render::text::extract_preedit_underlines：对变化的可编辑文字，读取预编辑下划线布局矩形，应用内容盒位置、编辑视口偏移及文字裁剪，使用文字颜色生成对应绘制项；不可见、空节点或无下划线时跳过。 参数范围：主世界；只读声明。
bevy_ui_render::debug_overlay::extract_debug_overlay：结合全局与逐节点调试配置，为边框盒、内边距盒、内容盒以及滚动条槽和滑块生成轮廓渲染节点，置于普通 UI 上方；按设置决定是否显示隐藏或被裁剪部分，并支持指定或按实体分配颜色。 参数范围：主世界；只读声明。
bevy_ui_render::extract_inline_images：对变化且可见的非空文字节点，读取布局中的 InlineBox 矩形与 InlineImage，按内容盒位置转换到 UI 世界坐标，保留颜色、翻转、裁剪及层次，跳过透明或空图像。 参数范围：主世界；只读声明。

schedule-access-9029acdf309c9e4e.name: Assets<Image>
schedule-access-9029acdf309c9e4e.description: 以索引密集存储或 UUID 映射保存指定类型的资产，管理资产句柄，并在集合变化时暂存相应 AssetEvent。 本实例类型参数为 bevy_image::image::Image。
schedule-access-9029acdf309c9e4e.display_summary: 按资产身份存储对象并暂存变化消息。
fields:
源码文档：Stores [`Asset`] values identified by their [`AssetId`].

Assets identified by [`AssetId::Index`] will be stored in a "dense" vec-like storage. This is more efficient, but it means that
the assets can only be identified at runtime. This is the default behavior.

Assets identified by [`AssetId::Uuid`] will be stored in a hashmap. This is less efficient, but it means that the assets can be referenced
at compile time.

This tracks (and queues) [`AssetEvent`] events whenever changes to the collection occur.
To check whether the asset used by a given component has changed (due to a change in the handle or the underlying asset)
use the [`AssetChanged`](crate::asset_changed::AssetChanged) query filter.

声明字段／枚举项：
dense_storage: DenseAssetStorage<A>,
    hash_map: HashMap<Uuid, A>,
    handle_provider: AssetHandleProvider,
    queued_events: Vec<AssetEvent<A>>,
    /// Assets managed by the `Assets` struct with live strong `Handle`s
    /// originating from `get_strong_handle`.
    duplicate_handles: HashMap<AssetIndex, u16>,
本实例类型参数：bevy_image::image::Image
已核实使用场景：bevy_winit::cursor::update_cursors：处理 CursorIcon 的变化与待重试窗口，准备原生或自定义光标；自定义图像按裁切、翻转和热点生成或复用缓存，资源尚未加载时保留重试。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_egui::free_egui_textures_system：消费 Egui 纹理释放增量，从托管纹理表及图像资产集合移除相应托管纹理；同时读取图像移除消息，清除引用该资产的 Egui 用户纹理登记。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_render::camera::camera_system：响应窗口创建、尺寸与缩放变化及图像目标变化，更新 Camera 与 Projection 的目标尺寸和投影信息；只读取相机实际引用的图像目标。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_asset::assets::Assets<bevy_image::image::Image>::asset_events：将 Assets 暂存的 Added、Modified、Removed 等变化批量写入对应 AssetEvent 消息；存在 AssetChanges 时同步记录当前系统 tick，随后清空待发队列。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_sprite::calculate_bounds_2d：从 Mesh2d 资产包围盒或精灵的尺寸、图集区域及锚点计算 Aabb；新实体排入组件插入，已有包围盒并行更新，缺少必需资产时等待后续处理。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_ui::widget::inline_image::update_inline_image_boxes：图像组件或图像资产变化时解析实际尺寸；资源存在且尺寸有限、正数时建立随文本流动的 InlineBox，否则把盒子设为零尺寸并移出文本流。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_ui::widget::text::text_system：文本节点尺寸、字形提示或重排标志变化时，通过 TextPipeline 重算排版并写入 TextLayoutInfo；同时更新字体图集，等待测量函数的文本暂不排版。 参数范围：main；可变声明。

fields:
源码文档：Stores [`Asset`] values identified by their [`AssetId`].

Assets identified by [`AssetId::Index`] will be stored in a "dense" vec-like storage. This is more efficient, but it means that
the assets can only be identified at runtime. This is the default behavior.

Assets identified by [`AssetId::Uuid`] will be stored in a hashmap. This is less efficient, but it means that the assets can be referenced
at compile time.

This tracks (and queues) [`AssetEvent`] events whenever changes to the collection occur.
To check whether the asset used by a given component has changed (due to a change in the handle or the underlying asset)
use the [`AssetChanged`](crate::asset_changed::AssetChanged) query filter.

dense_storage: DenseAssetStorage<A>,
    hash_map: HashMap<Uuid, A>,
    handle_provider: AssetHandleProvider,
    queued_events: Vec<AssetEvent<A>>,
    /// Assets managed by the `Assets` struct with live strong `Handle`s
    /// originating from `get_strong_handle`.
    duplicate_handles: HashMap<AssetIndex, u16>,
本实例类型参数：bevy_image::texture_atlas::TextureAtlasLayout

schedule-access-d70d3770b9072f34.description: 记录应用启动以来的帧计数，在 Last 调度中递增，超过 u32 上限后回绕。

fields:
源码文档：Maintains a count of frames rendered since the start of the application.

[`FrameCount`] is incremented during [`Last`], providing predictable
behavior: it will be 0 during the first update, 1 during the next, and so forth.

# Overflows

[`FrameCount`] will wrap to 0 after exceeding [`u32::MAX`]. Within reasonable
assumptions, one may exploit wrapping arithmetic to determine the number of frames
that have elapsed between two observations – see [`u32::wrapping_sub()`].
已核实使用场景：bevy_diagnostic::frame_count::update_frame_count：对 FrameCount 使用回绕加法增加一帧，超过 u32 上限后从零继续，避免计数溢出导致异常。 参数范围：main；可变声明。

schedule-access-19a370b559a109f2.name: Messages<WindowCloseRequested>
schedule-access-19a370b559a109f2.description: 保存最近两次轮换期间产生的指定类型消息。各 MessageReader 独立维护读取进度，消息写入和读取顺序由调度决定。 本实例类型参数为 bevy_window::event::WindowCloseRequested。 消息载荷为 bevy_window::event::WindowCloseRequested。
fields:
源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

fields:
源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

源码文档：New-type for [`HashSet`](hb::HashSet) with [`FixedHasher`] as the default hashing provider.
Can be trivially converted to and from a [hashbrown] [`HashSet`](hb::HashSet) using [`From`].

A new-type is used instead of a type alias due to critical methods like [`new`](hb::HashSet::new)
being incompatible with Bevy's choice of default hasher.

Unlike [`hashbrown::HashSet`], [`HashSet`] defaults to [`FixedHasher`]
instead of [`RandomState`](crate::hash::RandomState).
This provides determinism by default with an acceptable compromise to denial
of service resistance in the context of a game engine.

源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)

This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,

[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

schedule-access-8f53b5a1e6267c9a.name: ConstraintGraph
schedule-access-8f53b5a1e6267c9a.description: 把共享刚体不能并行的接触流形分配到不同颜色；同色约束可并行求解，无法分色的溢出约束串行处理。
schedule-access-8f53b5a1e6267c9a.display_summary: 为并行接触求解维护约束着色图。
fields:
源码文档：The constraint graph used for graph coloring to solve constraints in parallel.

The graph holds up to [`GRAPH_COLOR_COUNT`] colors, where each [`GraphColor`] is a set of bodies and constraints
that can be solved in parallel without race conditions. Each body can appear in a given color only once.

The last color, [`COLOR_OVERFLOW_INDEX`], is used for constraints that cannot find a color.
They are solved serially on a single thread.

Each [`ContactManifold`] is considered to be a separate edge, because each manifold has its own [`ContactConstraint`].

See the [module-level documentation](self) for more general information about graph coloring.

[`ContactManifold`]: crate::collision::contact_types::ContactManifold
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::apply_contact_status_changes：排空窄相记录的接触状态变化，逐项维护约束与岛连接，汇总受到影响的休眠岛；唤醒名单排序去重后通过 WakeIslands 命令统一应用。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::prepare_contact_constraints：清空上一轮约束，按图颜色并行处理接触流形；跳过不生成约束、缺少刚体及双方均非动态的对，结合惯量、相对速度和柔度生成非空接触约束并汇总数量。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::solve_restitution：遍历接触约束，按恢复系数、速度阈值和配置迭代次数对求解器刚体施加恢复冲量；溢出约束串行处理，其余按约束颜色并行处理。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::store_contact_impulses：逐接触流形把法向和切向约束冲量写回 ContactGraph，同时记录法向总冲量以供碰撞数据查询，避免下轮从零开始求解已有接触。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::warm_start：按 warm_start_coefficient 把上一帧或子步保存的接触冲量重新应用到求解器刚体，作为约束求解初始值；溢出约束串行、其他颜色并行处理。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::solve_contacts<true>：迭代接触约束并向碰撞刚体施加冲量；泛型 USE_BIAS 决定是否加入重叠修正，用带偏置求解和无偏置松弛分别处理穿透与速度过冲。 参数范围：main；可变声明。

schedule-access-68883227e62d0b98.name: PhysicsIslands
schedule-access-68883227e62d0b98.description: 保存物理岛集合、接触节点和关节节点，支持连接变化后的合并、候选拆分与整岛休眠／唤醒判断。
schedule-access-68883227e62d0b98.display_summary: 管理模拟岛及接触和关节连接。
fields: 源码文档：A resource for the [`PhysicsIsland`]s in the simulation.
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::apply_contact_status_changes：排空窄相记录的接触状态变化，逐项维护约束与岛连接，汇总受到影响的休眠岛；唤醒名单排序去重后通过 WakeIslands 命令统一应用。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::islands::split_island：物理岛存在待拆分候选时，根据刚体碰撞体、接触图和关节图重新划分该岛，并更新刚体所属岛；拆分用于随后正确决定休眠。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::apply_joint_graph_changes：读取关节图新增和移除消息，连接或解除对应岛节点，并请求唤醒受影响的休眠岛；已失效的关节变化会跳过，未启用物理岛时只清空消息。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::islands::sleeping::update_sleeping_states：线速度和角速度低于阈值时累计 SleepTimer，否则归零；未达到等待时间的刚体将整岛标为保持清醒。已够静止但有约束移除的岛会被选为后续拆分候选。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::islands::sleeping::wake_all_islands：收集 is_sleeping 的岛并排入 WakeIslands 命令，没有休眠岛时不发命令；用于重力等全局变化后使物体重新参与模拟。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::islands::sleeping::sleep_islands：依据活跃岛位图和待拆分状态收集需要休眠或唤醒的物理岛，通过 World 命令应用状态变化，并同步岛内刚体的休眠状态。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
usageContexts: avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::apply_contact_status_changes：排空窄相记录的接触状态变化，逐项维护约束与岛连接，汇总受到影响的休眠岛；唤醒名单排序去重后通过 WakeIslands 命令统一应用。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::solver::islands::split_island：物理岛存在待拆分候选时，根据刚体碰撞体、接触图和关节图重新划分该岛，并更新刚体所属岛；拆分用于随后正确决定休眠。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::apply_joint_graph_changes：读取关节图新增和移除消息，连接或解除对应岛节点，并请求唤醒受影响的休眠岛；已失效的关节变化会跳过，未启用物理岛时只清空消息。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::solver::islands::sleeping::update_sleeping_states：线速度和角速度低于阈值时累计 SleepTimer，否则归零；未达到等待时间的刚体将整岛标为保持清醒。已够静止但有约束移除的岛会被选为后续拆分候选。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::solver::islands::sleeping::wake_all_islands：收集 is_sleeping 的岛并排入 WakeIslands 命令，没有休眠岛时不发命令；用于重力等全局变化后使物体重新参与模拟。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
avian3d::dynamics::solver::islands::sleeping::sleep_islands：依据活跃岛位图和待拆分状态收集需要休眠或唤醒的物理岛，通过 World 命令应用状态变化，并同步岛内刚体的休眠状态。 参数范围：main；可变声明。

schedule-access-3089e5fcd79538c9.description: 保存两端参考框架以约束相对平移与旋转；该约束通过迭代求解，可配置刚度并读取连接力，仍可能存在数值误差。
schedule-access-3089e5fcd79538c9.display_summary: 锁定两刚体的相对位姿。
fields:
源码文档：A fixed [joint](dynamics::joints) prevents any relative movement between two bodies, effectively locking them together. This can be useful for cases where attaching multiple colliders to a single body is not enough, for example when you need to read forces applied by the joint to determine when the connection should break.
Due to the nature of iterative solvers, fixed joints can still have some error and allow small relative movement, even when using infinite stiffness. If you do not need features such as stiffness or reading back forces, consider attaching multiple colliders to a single rigid body instead. This is more efficient and stable than using joints.
Each fixed joint is defined by a [`JointFrame`] on each body. The joint aims to keep the anchor point and basis of each frame aligned, locking them together.

schedule-access-c50821d7ac12dfe5.description: 保存最近两次轮换期间产生的指定类型消息。各 MessageReader 独立维护读取进度，消息写入和读取顺序由调度决定。 本实例类型参数为 avian3d::dynamics::joints::joint_graph::plugin::JointGraphChange。 消息载荷为 avian3d::dynamics::joints::joint_graph::plugin::JointGraphChange。
fields:
源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

[`MessageReader`]: super::MessageReader
[`MessageWriter`]: super::MessageWriter
[`message_update_system`]: super::message_update_system

fields:
源码文档：A marker component for [rigid bodies](RigidBody) whose velocities should be projected
from the position corrections applied by XPBD constraints.

The XPBD solver only stores pre-solve deltas and projects velocities for bodies with this
component, so bodies that no XPBD constraint touches are skipped entirely.

This is inserted and removed automatically for the bodies of joints in the [`JointGraph`].
If you implement a [custom XPBD constraint](crate::dynamics::solver::xpbd#custom-constraints)
that is not registered in the joint graph, insert this component on the participating bodies
yourself, or the constraint will have no effect on their velocities.

[`JointGraph`]: crate::dynamics::joints::joint_graph::JointGraph

fields:
源码文档：A prismatic [joint](dynamics::joints) prevents any relative movement between two bodies,
except for translation along the [`slider_axis`](Self::slider_axis).

This can be useful for things like elevators, pistons, sliding doors and moving platforms.

Each prismatic joint is defined by a [`JointFrame`] on each body, a [`slider_axis`](Self::slider_axis)
along which the bodies can translate, and an optional [`DistanceLimit`] that defines the extents
of the allowed translation.


The joint can also include a [`LinearMotor`] for driving the translation along the [`slider_axis`](Self::slider_axis).
Use this to create pistons, elevators, or other linear motion mechanisms.

schedule-access-0d4f4f11cb4a9ffc.name: SphericalJoint
schedule-access-0d4f4f11cb4a9ffc.description: 约束两刚体相对平移，同时允许各轴旋转；可用扭转轴、扭转限制及摆动限制约束可转动范围。
schedule-access-0d4f4f11cb4a9ffc.display_summary: 保持球铰锚点重合并允许转动。
fields:
源码文档：A spherical [joint](dynamics::joints) prevents any relative translation between two bodies,
while allowing limited rotation about all axes.

This is similar to the ball-and-socket joint in the human shoulder, and can be useful for things like ragdolls, robotic arms,
pendula, chains, and other mechanisms where you need to allow free rotation around a point.

Each spherical joint is defined by a [`JointFrame`] on each body. The joint aims to keep the anchor point of each frame aligned,
while allowing free rotation.


The relative rotation can optionally be limited to a circular cone defined by a [`twist_axis`](Self::twist_axis) about which the bodies can twist,
a [`twist_limit`](Self::twist_limit) that defines the extents of the allowed twisting, and a [`swing_limit`](Self::swing_limit) that defines the extents
of the allowed swing as a half-angle.

fields:
源码文档：The Axis-Aligned Bounding Box of a [collider](Collider) in world space.

This is updated automatically.

# Large Worlds

When the `f64` feature is enabled, the AABB still uses
single-precision coordinates for BVH performance reasons,
but rounds outward to ensure that it encompasses the collider.
When the shape is far from the origin, its bounds may become more
conservative and inflated due to the limited precision of `f32`.

At `1e7` units from the origin, the floating-point quantization
is about one unit, while at `1e8` units from the origin, it is
about sixteen units. The simulation should still behave correctly,
but the effectiveness of the broad phase and its acceleration structures
may be reduced, as they will report more false positives. It is recommended
to remain within `1e7` to `1e8` units from the origin to not degrade
broad phase performance too much.

fields:
源码文档：The margin used to enlarge the [`ColliderAabb`] of a collider into its [`EnlargedAabb`].

Enlarging the AABB allows the collider to move by a small amount without triggering
an update of the [`ColliderTree`], which improves performance.

The margin is computed automatically from the size of the collider, scaled relative to the
[`PhysicsLengthUnit`]. Larger shapes get a larger margin (up to [`ColliderAabbMargin::MAX`]),
while small shapes get a margin proportional to their size to avoid wastefully fat AABBs.

[`ColliderTree`]: crate::collider_tree::ColliderTree
[`PhysicsLengthUnit`]: crate::dynamics::solver::PhysicsLengthUnit

```
schedule-access-e279e4993dd27b58.display_summary: 追踪后台碰撞体树优化任务。
fields:
源码文档：A resource tracking the ongoing optimization of [`ColliderTree`]s.

All trees are optimized by a single task, one after another,
to leave as many threads as possible for the narrow phase and solver.
The jobs are still claimed individually, so [`finish_optimize_trees`]
can pick up the ones the task has not reached yet and run them alongside it.

声明字段／枚举项：
jobs: Vec<Arc<OptimizationJob>>,
    task: Option<Task<()>>,

已核实使用场景：avian3d::collider_tree::optimization::finish_optimize_trees：接手后台尚未开始的优化作业；仍有作业执行时等待任务完成，然后把各作业的 BVH 和工作区写回对应树并累计优化耗时。没有任务时直接返回。 参数范围：main；可变声明。

fields:
源码文档：A system parameter for managing the narrow phase.

Responsibilities:

- Updates each active [`ContactPair`] in the [`ContactGraph`].
- Sends [collision events](crate::collision::collision_events) when colliders start or stop touching.
- Removes contact pairs from the [`ContactGraph`] when AABBs stop overlapping.
- Records [`ContactStatusChange`]s for the solver when contacts start or stop generating contact manifolds.

[`ConstraintGraph`]: crate::dynamics::solver::constraint_graph::ConstraintGraph
[`PhysicsIslands`]: crate::dynamics::solver::islands::PhysicsIslands

声明字段／枚举项：
collider_query: Query<'w, 's, ColliderQuery<C>, Without<ColliderDisabled>>,
    colliding_entities_query: Query<'w, 's, &'static mut CollidingEntities>,
    body_query: Query<'w, 's, RigidBodyQuery, Without<RigidBodyDisabled>>,
    pub contact_graph: ResMut<'w, ContactGraph>,
    /// The queue of contact status changess.
    pub contact_status_changes: ResMut<'w, ContactStatusChangeQueue>,
    contact_status_bits: ResMut<'w, ContactStatusBits>,
    #[cfg(feature = "parallel")]
    thread_locals: ResMut<'w, NarrowPhaseThreadLocals>,
    pub config: Res<'w, NarrowPhaseConfig>,
    default_friction: Res<'w, DefaultFriction>,
    default_restitution: Res<'w, DefaultRestitution>,
    length_unit: Res<'w, PhysicsLengthUnit>,

schedule-access-3ca8c6dac37be822.name: VelocityIntegrationData
schedule-access-3ca8c6dac37be822.description: 累加线性与角加速度，准备阶段乘时间步转成每子步速度增量，并保存阻尼方程系数供积分阶段重复使用。
schedule-access-3ca8c6dac37be822.display_summary: 缓存子步速度增量和阻尼系数。
fields: 已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::integrator::clear_velocity_increments：并行清空具有求解器索引的刚体的线性及角速度增量，并累计清理耗时，防止本轮累加作用沿用到下一物理步。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::rigid_body::forces::plugin::apply_constant_forces：用 ComputedMass 的逆质量乘 ConstantForce，累加到线性积分数据；不同质量的刚体会得到不同加速度，时间步换算留给后续预处理。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::rigid_body::forces::plugin::apply_constant_torques：通过 SolverBodyIndex 读取当前求解器惯性数据，把 ConstantTorque 转成待积分角加速度；索引没有对应惯性数据时跳过。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::rigid_body::forces::plugin::apply_constant_linear_acceleration：将 ConstantLinearAcceleration 直接累加到线性积分数据，不经过质量换算，随后与其他加速度一起按子步时长积分。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::rigid_body::forces::plugin::apply_constant_angular_acceleration：将 ConstantAngularAcceleration 直接累加到 VelocityIntegrationData 的角增量；此时增量仍表示加速度，后续预处理才乘子步时长。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::integrator::pre_process_velocity_increments：仅处理动态刚体：先按阻尼系数和子步时长缓存衰减因子，累加带 GravityScale 的重力，再屏蔽锁定轴，最后乘时间步把加速度转为速度增量。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::integrator::integrate_velocities：对采用默认速度积分的活跃动态刚体，先应用线性和角速度阻尼，再累加当前步的速度增量；运动学刚体跳过该积分，并记录诊断耗时。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
usageContexts: avian3d::dynamics::integrator::clear_velocity_increments：并行清空具有求解器索引的刚体的线性及角速度增量，并累计清理耗时，防止本轮累加作用沿用到下一物理步。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::rigid_body::forces::plugin::apply_constant_forces：用 ComputedMass 的逆质量乘 ConstantForce，累加到线性积分数据；不同质量的刚体会得到不同加速度，时间步换算留给后续预处理。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::rigid_body::forces::plugin::apply_constant_torques：通过 SolverBodyIndex 读取当前求解器惯性数据，把 ConstantTorque 转成待积分角加速度；索引没有对应惯性数据时跳过。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::rigid_body::forces::plugin::apply_constant_linear_acceleration：将 ConstantLinearAcceleration 直接累加到线性积分数据，不经过质量换算，随后与其他加速度一起按子步时长积分。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::rigid_body::forces::plugin::apply_constant_angular_acceleration：将 ConstantAngularAcceleration 直接累加到 VelocityIntegrationData 的角增量；此时增量仍表示加速度，后续预处理才乘子步时长。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::integrator::pre_process_velocity_increments：仅处理动态刚体：先按阻尼系数和子步时长缓存衰减因子，累加带 GravityScale 的重力，再屏蔽锁定轴，最后乘时间步把加速度转为速度增量。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::integrator::integrate_velocities：对采用默认速度积分的活跃动态刚体，先应用线性和角速度阻尼，再累加当前步的速度增量；运动学刚体跳过该积分，并记录诊断耗时。 参数范围：main；可变声明。

schedule-access-411d151dd54ea0fc.name: SolverBodyIndex
schedule-access-411d151dd54ea0fc.description: 组件索引指向 SolverBodies，只为醒着的动态和运动学刚体自动维护；静态或休眠动态刚体使用占位状态。
schedule-access-411d151dd54ea0fc.display_summary: 定位实体对应的求解器刚体。
fields:
源码文档：A component storing the index of an entity's [`SolverBody`] in the [`SolverBodies`] resource.

Only awake dynamic and kinematic bodies have an associated solver body.
Static bodies and sleeping dynamic bodies do not have a solver body, and instead
use a "dummy state" with [`SolverBody::default()`] and [`SolverBodyInertia::default()`].

This component is added, removed, and updated automatically by the solver plugin,
and should not be modified by users.
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::integrator::clear_velocity_increments：并行清空具有求解器索引的刚体的线性及角速度增量，并累计清理耗时，防止本轮累加作用沿用到下一物理步。 参数范围：main；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::solver_body::plugin::writeback_solver_bodies：合并求解体的平移和旋转增量，并用旋转前后的局部质心偏移修正位置，使物体绕质心转动；随后写回线速度和角速度，并记录回写耗时。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::solver_body::plugin::prepare_solver_bodies：复制速度、清零本轮位姿增量，并按世界旋转、总质量和惯量、轴锁与支配等级准备惯性状态；同时设置运动学、自定义位姿积分和三维陀螺运动标志。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::rigid_body::forces::plugin::apply_constant_torques：通过 SolverBodyIndex 读取当前求解器惯性数据，把 ConstantTorque 转成待积分角加速度；索引没有对应惯性数据时跳过。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::ccd::solve_continuous：对单步位移相对厚度过大的动态刚体执行连续碰撞扫掠；发现碰撞时缩短累计运动，使刚体停在首次撞击位置，并保留后续接触处理所需信息。 参数范围：main；只读声明。

已核实使用场景：avian3d::collider_tree::update::update_solver_body_aabbs<avian3d::collision::collider::parry::Collider>：遍历醒着的动态和运动学求解体，更新其附着碰撞体 AABB；启用 SpeculativeCcd 时按线速度、旋转及质心偏移扩展预测运动。越出扩大边界的代理更新树位置，并记录更新刻度和耗时。 参数范围：main；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::islands::sleeping::update_sleeping_states：线速度和角速度低于阈值时累计 SleepTimer，否则归零；未达到等待时间的刚体将整岛标为保持清醒。已够静止但有约束移除的岛会被选为后续拆分候选。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::rigid_body::forces::plugin::apply_local_acceleration：对未使用自定义速度积分的刚体，结合起始旋转与本子步旋转增量转换局部线／角加速度，屏蔽锁定轴后乘子步时长并更新求解器速度。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::integrator::integrate_velocities：对采用默认速度积分的活跃动态刚体，先应用线性和角速度阻尼，再累加当前步的速度增量；运动学刚体跳过该积分，并记录诊断耗时。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::integrator::clamp_velocities：分别按 MaxLinearSpeed 和 MaxAngularSpeed 限制求解器刚体的速度大小，超过上限时保持方向缩放；线速度和角速度查询通过 ParamSet 分开访问。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::solver_body::plugin::update_solver_body_angular_inertia：通过每个刚体的求解器索引，把 ComputedAngularInertia 旋转到当前朝向并更新有效逆角惯量，使后续旋转约束使用当前世界方向上的响应。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::joint_damping<avian3d::dynamics::joints::fixed::FixedJoint>：读取指定关节及 JointDamping，查找两端刚体的求解器索引并按时间步修正相对速度；静态端使用占位刚体，同一索引不重复处理。 参数范围：main；只读声明。

schedule-access-8fa08522e07cda0f.name: SolverDiagnostics
schedule-access-8fa08522e07cda0f.description: 分别累计约束准备、速度增量更新、积分、热启动及约束求解等耗时，供物理诊断汇总求解成本。
schedule-access-8fa08522e07cda0f.display_summary: 记录物理求解各阶段耗时。
fields: 源码文档：Diagnostics for the physics solver.
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::integrator::clear_velocity_increments：并行清空具有求解器索引的刚体的线性及角速度增量，并累计清理耗时，防止本轮累加作用沿用到下一物理步。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::solver_body::plugin::writeback_solver_bodies：合并求解体的平移和旋转增量，并用旋转前后的局部质心偏移修正位置，使物体绕质心转动；随后写回线速度和角速度，并记录回写耗时。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::prepare_contact_constraints：清空上一轮约束，按图颜色并行处理接触流形；跳过不生成约束、缺少刚体及双方均非动态的对，结合惯量、相对速度和柔度生成非空接触约束并汇总数量。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::integrator::pre_process_velocity_increments：仅处理动态刚体：先按阻尼系数和子步时长缓存衰减因子，累加带 GravityScale 的重力，再屏蔽锁定轴，最后乘时间步把加速度转为速度增量。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::solve_restitution：遍历接触约束，按恢复系数、速度阈值和配置迭代次数对求解器刚体施加恢复冲量；溢出约束串行处理，其余按约束颜色并行处理。 参数范围：main；可变声明。

已核实使用场景：<avian3d::dynamics::solver::diagnostics::SolverDiagnostics as avian3d::diagnostics::PhysicsDiagnostics>::reset：清零当前物理诊断类型的计数及耗时采样，准备记录下一次物理步。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::rigid_body::forces::plugin::apply_local_acceleration：对未使用自定义速度积分的刚体，结合起始旋转与本子步旋转增量转换局部线／角加速度，屏蔽锁定轴后乘子步时长并更新求解器速度。 参数范围：main；可变声明。

已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::integrator::clamp_velocities：分别按 MaxLinearSpeed 和 MaxAngularSpeed 限制求解器刚体的速度大小，超过上限时保持方向缩放；线速度和角速度查询通过 ParamSet 分开访问。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::integrator::integrate_positions：依据求解器刚体速度与本子步时间累加 delta_position 和 delta_rotation；带自定义位置积分标志的刚体跳过默认积分。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::warm_start：按 warm_start_coefficient 把上一帧或子步保存的接触冲量重新应用到求解器刚体，作为约束求解初始值；溢出约束串行、其他颜色并行处理。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::solve_contacts<true>：迭代接触约束并向碰撞刚体施加冲量；泛型 USE_BIAS 决定是否加入重叠修正，用带偏置求解和无偏置松弛分别处理穿透与速度过冲。 参数范围：main；可变声明。

avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::store_contact_impulses：逐接触流形把法向和切向约束冲量写回 ContactGraph，同时记录法向总冲量以供碰撞数据查询，避免下轮从零开始求解已有接触。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
<avian3d::dynamics::solver::diagnostics::SolverDiagnostics as avian3d::diagnostics::PhysicsDiagnostics>::reset：清零当前物理诊断类型的计数及耗时采样，准备记录下一次物理步。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::rigid_body::forces::plugin::apply_local_acceleration：对未使用自定义速度积分的刚体，结合起始旋转与本子步旋转增量转换局部线／角加速度，屏蔽锁定轴后乘子步时长并更新求解器速度。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::integrator::integrate_velocities：对采用默认速度积分的活跃动态刚体，先应用线性和角速度阻尼，再累加当前步的速度增量；运动学刚体跳过该积分，并记录诊断耗时。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::integrator::clamp_velocities：分别按 MaxLinearSpeed 和 MaxAngularSpeed 限制求解器刚体的速度大小，超过上限时保持方向缩放；线速度和角速度查询通过 ParamSet 分开访问。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::integrator::integrate_positions：依据求解器刚体速度与本子步时间累加 delta_position 和 delta_rotation；带自定义位置积分标志的刚体跳过默认积分。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::warm_start：按 warm_start_coefficient 把上一帧或子步保存的接触冲量重新应用到求解器刚体，作为约束求解初始值；溢出约束串行、其他颜色并行处理。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::solve_contacts<true>：迭代接触约束并向碰撞刚体施加冲量；泛型 USE_BIAS 决定是否加入重叠修正，用带偏置求解和无偏置松弛分别处理穿透与速度过冲。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
avian3d::dynamics::solver::plugin::solve_contacts<false>：迭代接触约束并向碰撞刚体施加冲量；泛型 USE_BIAS 决定是否加入重叠修正，用带偏置求解和无偏置松弛分别处理穿透与速度过冲。 参数范围：main；可变声明。

源码文档：A resource storing [solver bodies](SolverBody) and their [inertial properties](SolverBodyInertia)
contiguously for awake, active rigid bodies.

Each entity with a solver body stores an index into this resource in a [`SolverBodyIndex`] component.

声明字段／枚举项：
// TODO: Use `UniqueEntityVec`.
    entities: Vec<Entity>,
    bodies: Vec<SolverBody>,
    inertias: Vec<SolverBodyInertia>,
已核实使用场景：avian3d::dynamics::solver::solver_body::plugin::writeback_solver_bodies：合并求解体的平移和旋转增量，并用旋转前后的局部质心偏移修正位置，使物体绕质心转动；随后写回线速度和角速度，并记录回写耗时。 参数范围：main；只读声明。

schedule-access-3da308e20280c7ab.name: ComputedCenterOfMass
schedule-access-3da308e20280c7ab.description: 按质量加权平均刚体自身与附着碰撞体、后代的质心，供位姿回写、连续扫掠和接触杠杆臂计算使用。
schedule-access-3da308e20280c7ab.display_summary: 保存汇总后的刚体局部质心。
fields:
源码文档：The local [center of mass] computed for a dynamic [rigid body], taking into account
colliders and descendants. Represents the average position of mass in the body.

The total center of mass is computed as the weighted average of the centers of mass
of all attached colliders and the center of mass of the rigid body entity itself.
The center of mass of an entity is determined by its [`CenterOfMass`] component,
or if it is not present, from an attached [`Collider`] based on its shape.

[center of mass]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_of_mass
[rigid body]: RigidBody

# Related Types

- [`CenterOfMass`] can be used to set the local center of mass associated with an individual entity.
- [`ComputedMass`] stores the total mass of a rigid body, taking into account colliders and descendants.
- [`ComputedAngularInertia`] stores the total angular inertia of a rigid body, taking into account colliders and descendants.
- [`MassPropertyHelper`] is a [`SystemParam`] with utilities for computing and updating mass properties.

[`SystemParam`]: bevy::ecs::system::SystemParam

schedule-access-7491501f7c4228c4.name: ConstantForce
schedule-access-7491501f7c4228c4.description: 保存持续作用于动态刚体的力，积分阶段结合总质量转为线性加速度并与其他作用累加，适合恒定推力等外力。
fields:
源码文档：A component for applying a constant force to a dynamic rigid body in world space.
The unit is typically N or kg⋅m/s².

The force persists across time steps, and is accumulated with other forces.
This can be useful for simulating constant forces like gravity, force fields, wind,
or other environmental effects.

See the [module-level documentation](self) for more general information about forces in Avian.

# Example

```
# use bevy::prelude::*;
#
# fn setup(mut commands: Commands) {
commands.spawn((
    RigidBody::Dynamic,
    Collider::capsule(0.5, 1.0),
    // Apply a constant force of 10 N in the positive Y direction.
));
# }
```

# Related Types

- [`Forces`]: A helper [`QueryData`](bevy::ecs::query::QueryData) for applying forces, impulses, and acceleration to entities.
- [`ConstantLocalForce`]: Applies a constant force in local space.
- [`ConstantTorque`]: Applies a constant torque in world space.
- [`ConstantLinearAcceleration`]: Applies a constant linear acceleration in world space.
- [`ConstantAngularAcceleration`]: Applies a constant angular acceleration in world space.
```

fields:
源码文档：A component for applying a constant torque to a dynamic rigid body in local space.
The unit is typically N⋅m or kg⋅m²/s²

The torque persists across time steps, and is accumulated with other torques.
This can be useful for simulating constant torques like torque from a motor,
or other rotational effects in local space.

See the [module-level documentation](self) for more general information about forces in Avian.

# Example

```
# use avian3d::prelude::*;
# use bevy::prelude::*;
#
# fn setup(mut commands: Commands) {
commands.spawn((
    RigidBody::Dynamic,
    Collider::capsule(0.5, 1.0),
    // Apply a constant torque of 5 N⋅m in the positive Z direction in local space.
    ConstantLocalTorque::new(0.0, 0.0, 5.0),
));
# }
```

# Related Types

- [`Forces`]: A helper [`QueryData`](bevy::ecs::query::QueryData) for applying forces, impulses, and acceleration to entities.
- [`ConstantTorque`]: Applies a constant torque in world space.
- [`ConstantLocalForce`]: Applies a constant force in local space.
- [`ConstantLocalLinearAcceleration`]: Applies a constant linear acceleration in local space.
- [`ConstantLocalAngularAcceleration`]: Applies a constant angular acceleration in local space.

schedule-access-989a698196538cd0.name: SpeculativeCcd
schedule-access-989a698196538cd0.description: 启用速度扩大的 AABB 与预测碰撞余量，并以 max_distance 限制最远预测距离；扩大范围会增加候选接触及近似碰撞的风险。
schedule-access-989a698196538cd0.display_summary: 配置基于速度的预测接触范围。
fields:
源码文档：A component that enables [speculative collision](self#speculative-collision)
and velocity-expanded [AABBs](ColliderAabb) for a [`RigidBody`],
allowing it to predict and react to contacts before they happen.

Without this component, a body still receives a small, fixed [`contact_tolerance`]
and automatic [swept CCD](self#swept-ccd), but no velocity-based speculative margin
or AABB expansion.

Speculative collisions can be cheaper than swept CCD for highly dynamic scenes,
but are more approximate, and can cause [ghost collisions](self#caveats-of-speculative-collision).
The [`max_distance`](Self::max_distance) property bounds the margin to help mitigate this.

Read the [module-level documentation](self) for more information about what CCD is,
what it is used for, and what limitations and tradeoffs it can have.

[`contact_tolerance`]: NarrowPhaseConfig::contact_tolerance

# Example

```
use bevy::prelude::*;

fn setup(mut commands: Commands) {
    // A fast body that predicts contacts up to 2 units ahead based on its velocity,
    // expands its AABB accordingly, and is also swept against other dynamic bodies.
    commands.spawn((
        RigidBody::Dynamic,
        SpeculativeCcd::new(2.0),
        SweptCcd::default().with_filter(CcdFilter::ALL),
    ));
}
```

源码文档：An asynchronous MPSC channel that buffers messages and reuses allocations with thread locals.

This is a building block for efficient parallel worker tasks.

Cache this channel in a system's `Local` to reuse allocated memory.

This is faster than sending each message individually into a channel when communicating between
tasks. Unlike `Parallel`, this allows you to execute a consuming task while producing tasks are
concurrently sending data into the channel, enabling you to run a serial processing consumer
at the same time as many parallel processing producers.

schedule-access-73b4b8b9703880c1.description: 保存最近两次轮换期间产生的指定类型消息。各 MessageReader 独立维护读取进度，消息写入和读取顺序由调度决定。 本实例类型参数为 bevy_window::event::WindowCreated。 消息载荷为 bevy_window::event::WindowCreated。
fields:
源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

[`MessageReader`]: super::MessageReader
[`MessageWriter`]: super::MessageWriter
[`message_update_system`]: super::message_update_system

源码文档：Component that defines how to compute a [`Camera`]'s projection matrix.

Common projections, like perspective and orthographic, are provided out of the box to handle the
majority of use cases. Custom projections can be added using the [`CameraProjection`] trait and
the [`Projection::custom`] constructor.

## What's a projection?

A camera projection essentially describes how 3d points from the point of view of a camera are
projected onto a 2d screen. This is where properties like a camera's field of view are defined.
More specifically, a projection is a 4x4 matrix that transforms points from view space (the
point of view of the camera) into clip space. Clip space is almost, but not quite, equivalent to
the rectangle that is rendered to your screen, with a depth axis. Any points that land outside
the bounds of this cuboid are "clipped" and not rendered.

You can also think of the projection as the thing that describes the shape of a camera's
frustum: the volume in 3d space that is visible to a camera.

schedule-access-6ce73243f21861c6.display_summary: 保存当前输入焦点实体、待派发的焦点变化及原焦点
fields: 已核实使用场景：bevy_input_focus::set_initial_focus：当前 InputFocus 为空时，把可用的主窗口设为初始导航焦点；已有焦点时保持原目标。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_input_focus::gained_and_lost::process_recorded_focus_changes：逐项消费 InputFocus 的焦点变化记录，只有实体确实变化时才向旧目标触发 FocusLost、向新目标触发 FocusGained；同步内部原焦点快照但不再次修改对外当前焦点。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_winit::accessibility::update_accessibility_nodes：主窗口和 AccessKit 适配器可用时，依据输入焦点及变化的 AccessibilityNode 更新可访问性树；焦点指向尚未存在的实体时暂缓，只有已激活适配器才提交更新。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_ui::widget::text_input_layout::update_editable_text_layout：布局代数或字体提示变化时重建 TextLayoutInfo 的字形、行几何、选区和输入法预编辑下划线，并把所需字形加入图集；同时依据焦点和实时时钟更新光标闪烁，必要时显露光标并限制文本视口滚动范围。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_ui_widgets::menu::menu_acquire_focus：查找处于 Opening 的菜单，按记录的导航方向初始化第一个或最后一个可聚焦目标；成功后切换到 Open 并设置导航焦点，没有可聚焦菜单项时记录警告。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_ui_widgets::text_input::text_input_autoscroll_system：从焦点目标的主按钮拖动状态取得指针位置，转换到文字局部坐标，按越界距离、视口大小及帧时间计算滚动，限制在文字布局范围并同步拖动选择；组合输入法文本时不执行。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_ui_widgets::menu::menu_on_lose_focus：对已打开或正在打开的菜单，检查焦点是否为自身或后代；焦点移出或消失时把状态改为 Closed，并触发该菜单的 CloseAll 事件。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_ui_widgets::tabs::update_tablist_derived_state：验证 SelectedTab 必须指向启用的直接子标签，再同步 Selected 标记；按当前焦点、有效选择和第一个可用项的优先级选择唯一 TabIndex(0)，其余标签为 -1，实现标签栏的游走焦点导航。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_ui_widgets::text_input::update_ime_position：读取聚焦且可编辑目标的 Parley 光标或预编辑矩形，将其底边位置结合内容盒、文字滚动偏移、UI 变换及缩放换算为窗口坐标，更新主窗口 ime_position。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_input_focus::dispatch_focused_input<bevy_input::gamepad::GamepadButtonChangedEvent>：读取对应输入消息并向当前焦点实体派发可冒泡的 FocusedInput；焦点无效时回退到主窗口。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_input_focus::dispatch_focused_input<bevy_input::mouse::MouseWheel>：读取对应输入消息并向当前焦点实体派发可冒泡的 FocusedInput；焦点无效时回退到主窗口。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_ui_widgets::text_input::listen_for_ime_input_when_text_input_focused：检查当前焦点是否是允许编辑的 EditableText，据此设置主窗口 ime_enabled；文本模式改为只读或静态时排入清除输入法预编辑操作。 参数范围：main；只读声明。

源码文档：User indication of whether an entity is visible. Propagates down the entity hierarchy.

If an entity is hidden in this way, all [`Children`] (and all of their children and so on) who
are set to [`Inherited`](Self::Inherited) will also be hidden.

Users should set this component if they wish to change the visibility of an entity.

To read the visibility of an entity, query for its [`InheritedVisibility`] instead.
For more information, see [module level documentation](self#what-is-the-difference-between-visibility-components).

schedule-access-a6de264d282f5f80.description: 沿父子关系读取最新局部 Transform，按需计算包含尚未传播变动的 GlobalTransform。
schedule-access-a6de264d282f5f80.display_summary: 沿父子关系读取最新局部 Transform
fields:
源码文档：System parameter for computing up-to-date [`GlobalTransform`]s.

Computing an entity's [`GlobalTransform`] can be expensive so it is recommended
you use the [`GlobalTransform`] component stored on the entity, unless you need
a [`GlobalTransform`] that reflects the changes made to any [`Transform`]s since
the last time the transform propagation systems ran.

声明字段／枚举项：
parent_query: Query<'w, 's, &'static ChildOf>,
    transform_query: Query<'w, 's, &'static Transform>,

已核实使用场景：bevy_transform::systems::propagate_transforms_for<bevy_ecs::query::filter::Or<(bevy_ecs::query::filter::With<bevy_gizmos::transform_gizmo::TransformGizmoRoot>, bevy_ecs::query::filter::With<bevy_gizmos_render::transform_gizmo_render::GizmoOverlayCamera>, bevy_ecs::query::filter::With<bevy_gizmos::transform_gizmo::TransformGizmoMeshMarker>)>>：对匹配泛型过滤器的实体，通过 TransformHelper 沿层级计算当前 GlobalTransform，成功才写回；计算失败保留旧值，启用追踪时给出诊断，适合同帧移动后立即取用世界变换。 参数范围：main；参数或查询接口引用。

源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

[`MessageReader`]: super::MessageReader
[`MessageWriter`]: super::MessageWriter
[`message_update_system`]: super::message_update_system

schedule-access-fb8f0006a31bce41.name: Assets<LoadedUntypedAsset>
schedule-access-fb8f0006a31bce41.description: 以索引密集存储或 UUID 映射保存指定类型的资产，管理资产句柄，并在集合变化时暂存相应 AssetEvent。 本实例类型参数为 bevy_asset::assets::LoadedUntypedAsset。
schedule-access-fb8f0006a31bce41.display_summary: 按资产身份存储对象并暂存变化消息。
fields:
源码文档：Stores [`Asset`] values identified by their [`AssetId`].

Assets identified by [`AssetId::Index`] will be stored in a "dense" vec-like storage. This is more efficient, but it means that
the assets can only be identified at runtime. This is the default behavior.

Assets identified by [`AssetId::Uuid`] will be stored in a hashmap. This is less efficient, but it means that the assets can be referenced
at compile time.

This tracks (and queues) [`AssetEvent`] events whenever changes to the collection occur.
To check whether the asset used by a given component has changed (due to a change in the handle or the underlying asset)
use the [`AssetChanged`](crate::asset_changed::AssetChanged) query filter.

声明字段／枚举项：
dense_storage: DenseAssetStorage<A>,
    hash_map: HashMap<Uuid, A>,
    handle_provider: AssetHandleProvider,
    queued_events: Vec<AssetEvent<A>>,
    /// Assets managed by the `Assets` struct with live strong `Handle`s
    /// originating from `get_strong_handle`.
    duplicate_handles: HashMap<AssetIndex, u16>,

源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

the assets can only be identified at runtime. This is the default behavior.

at compile time.

use the [`AssetChanged`](crate::asset_changed::AssetChanged) query filter.

源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

[`MessageReader`]: super::MessageReader
[`MessageWriter`]: super::MessageWriter
[`message_update_system`]: super::message_update_system
