schedule-access-5e915d337ca73f39.name: Msaa
schedule-access-5e915d337ca73f39.description: 在关闭及二、四、八样本之间选择 MSAA 配置，供渲染纹理和管线准备使用；不兼容的延迟或顺序无关透明组合由检查系统处理。
schedule-access-5e915d337ca73f39.display_summary: 选择视图的多重采样抗锯齿样本数。
fields:
声明字段／枚举项：
Off = 1,
    Sample2 = 2,
    #[default]
    Sample4 = 4,
    Sample8 = 8,
已核实使用场景：bevy_core_pipeline::core_3d::check_msaa：检查带 DeferredPrepass 的相机，发现启用 MSAA 时发出警告并改为 Msaa::Off，避免延迟渲染使用不兼容的多重采样。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_core_pipeline::oit::check_msaa：检查启用了顺序无关透明设置的相机；若同时使用多于一个 MSAA 采样则直接报错，避免执行不受支持的透明渲染组合。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_post_process::msaa_writeback::msaa_writeback：在 MSAA 开启时把当前后处理颜色绘制回多采样主纹理，并解析到下一颜色目标，使后续通道继续使用一致的多采样附件；MSAA 关闭时跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_anti_alias::taa::temporal_anti_alias：在 MSAA 关闭且管线、深度和运动矢量均可用时，绑定当前颜色和历史纹理执行全屏时域抗锯齿，同时写入后处理颜色及下一历史纹理；条件不满足时跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_post_process::motion_blur::motion_blur：读取当前视图颜色、预通道运动矢量和深度，按快门角度及采样数执行运动模糊；采样关闭、所需纹理或管线不可用时跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::volumetric_fog::render::volumetric_fog：逐个处理视图中的体积雾区域，结合场景深度、光照和可选密度纹理绘制雾光照；根据相机位于雾体内外选择平面或立方体网格。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::ssao::extract_ssao_settings：读取带深度与法线预通道的三维相机；开启 MSAA 时记录不兼容错误并跳过，否则为活动相机复制遮蔽配置，为非活动相机移除该配置。 参数范围：主世界；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::prepass::specialize_prepass_material_meshes：为变化的可见网格组合采样、预通道、光照贴图、距离渐变及前帧蒙皮形变键，选择深度专用或材质绘制函数并缓存结果；清理禁用预通道、混合透明或读取透射纹理的旧专用化。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_render::view::composition::resolve_composition_spaces：按主纹理及相机顺序汇总空间请求并写回 ResolvedCompositingSpace；全部请求线性时直接归一化，冲突堆栈、非二维相机或 Oklab 缺少有符号存储时回退并警告，共享目标空间不一致时提示混合问题。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_sprite_render::mesh2d::mesh::check_views_need_specialization：根据采样数、目标格式、合成空间及 SDR 相机的着色器内色调映射和抖动设置生成视图键；与缓存不同时更新 ViewKeyCache，并将该视图加入 DirtySpecializations。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_render::view::prepare_view_targets：按相机目标、格式、用途及 MSAA 复用主颜色 A/B 纹理，将清除色转换到实际合成空间并关联输出附件；共享主纹理跨帧复用原子切换状态，无有效尺寸或无需输出的清除相机移除 ViewTarget。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_gizmos_render::pipeline_2d::queue_line_and_joint_gizmos_2d：按视图采样数、目标格式、渲染层及线条样式选择管线，把有效线段列表、线条带和接头加入二维透明阶段；无 GPU 网格、层不相交或顶点不足的部分跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_sprite_render::render::queue_sprites：按相机可见性筛选已提取精灵，结合目标格式、MSAA、色调映射和合成空间选择精灵管线，并将绘制项加入对应透明二维阶段。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::atmosphere::resources::queue_render_sky_pipelines：为具有大气的相机使用 MSAA 样本数和设备双源混合支持构造天空专用化键，取得或排队创建管线并插入 RenderSkyPipelineId。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_core_pipeline::core_2d::prepare_core_2d_depth_textures：在二维主阶段和物理目标尺寸有效时，按渲染目标复用深度纹理，使用相机 MSAA 采样数和二维深度格式，为视图插入深度附件。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_core_pipeline::core_3d::prepare_core_3d_depth_textures：合并同一相机目标所需的深度纹理用途，深度预通道额外要求 COPY_SRC；按目标及 MSAA 采样数复用纹理，并为各视图保存相机指定的深度清除或加载方式。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_core_pipeline::core_3d::prepare_prepass_textures：依据视图标记取得深度、法线、运动矢量、延迟 G-buffer 与光照通道标识纹理，按目标复用并按帧轮换双缓冲；运动矢量存储绑定受设备能力及单采样限制，无预通道阶段时移除旧纹理。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::render::mesh_view_bindings::prepare_mesh_view_bind_groups：按采样与预通道配置选择布局，将视图、光照、聚簇、阴影、探针、雾及透射和大气等资源组成主绑定与纹理数组绑定，保存动态偏移；缺省图像用于适当的替代纹理槽。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::atmosphere::resources::prepare_atmosphere_bind_groups：为大气三维视图建立四类查找表及天空绑定组，关联大气设置、散射介质、光照、坐标变换、查找纹理和视图深度；必需 Uniform 或介质缺失时返回错误，没有深度视图的对象跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_core_pipeline::skybox::prepare_skybox_pipelines：为带 Skybox 的渲染相机，以颜色目标格式、MSAA 采样数及三维深度格式专用化天空盒管线，将缓存标识附到相机。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_post_process::msaa_writeback::prepare_msaa_writeback_pipelines：按主纹理识别首个写入相机，结合 MSAA 回写开关、清除方式及是否后续全屏合成决定是否回写；需要时创建对应采样数和格式的 Blit 管线，否则移除旧回写组件。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_post_process::motion_blur::pipeline::prepare_motion_blur_pipelines：为带 MotionBlurUniform 的已提取相机，依据视图目标格式和 MSAA 采样数专用化运动模糊管线，将缓存标识附到相机。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_post_process::dof::prepare_depth_of_field_view_bind_group_layouts：按 MSAA 选择普通或多采样深度输入，并绑定视图参数和当前颜色；Bokeh 模式额外创建包含辅助颜色纹理的双输入布局，将两种布局附到视图。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_post_process::dof::prepare_depth_of_field_pipelines：结合视图绑定布局、全局布局、目标格式及 MSAA 状态，为 Gaussian 创建水平与垂直管线，为 Bokeh 创建第一和第二通道管线，将缓存标识写入视图。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。

已核实使用场景：bevy_core_pipeline::prepass::background_motion_vectors::prepare_background_motion_vectors_pipelines：对允许背景运动矢量的预通道视图，依据 MSAA 采样数及法线预通道开关专用化 BackgroundMotionVectorsPipeline，并保存逐视图缓存标识。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::prepass::check_prepass_views_need_specialization：将 MSAA、深度、法线及运动矢量预通道设置组合为视图键；首次出现或键发生变化时更新 ViewKeyPrepassCache，并把视图加入 DirtySpecializations。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::render::mesh::check_views_need_specialization：将格式、采样、预通道、投影、时间抖动、探针和反射、雾、大气、透射等设置组合为网格视图键，新建或变化时标记待专用化，并移除不再出现视图的缓存。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
usageContexts: bevy_core_pipeline::core_3d::check_msaa：检查带 DeferredPrepass 的相机，发现启用 MSAA 时发出警告并改为 Msaa::Off，避免延迟渲染使用不兼容的多重采样。 参数范围：main；可变声明。
bevy_core_pipeline::oit::check_msaa：检查启用了顺序无关透明设置的相机；若同时使用多于一个 MSAA 采样则直接报错，避免执行不受支持的透明渲染组合。 参数范围：main；只读声明。
bevy_post_process::msaa_writeback::msaa_writeback：在 MSAA 开启时把当前后处理颜色绘制回多采样主纹理，并解析到下一颜色目标，使后续通道继续使用一致的多采样附件；MSAA 关闭时跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_anti_alias::taa::temporal_anti_alias：在 MSAA 关闭且管线、深度和运动矢量均可用时，绑定当前颜色和历史纹理执行全屏时域抗锯齿，同时写入后处理颜色及下一历史纹理；条件不满足时跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_post_process::motion_blur::motion_blur：读取当前视图颜色、预通道运动矢量和深度，按快门角度及采样数执行运动模糊；采样关闭、所需纹理或管线不可用时跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::volumetric_fog::render::volumetric_fog：逐个处理视图中的体积雾区域，结合场景深度、光照和可选密度纹理绘制雾光照；根据相机位于雾体内外选择平面或立方体网格。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::ssao::extract_ssao_settings：读取带深度与法线预通道的三维相机；开启 MSAA 时记录不兼容错误并跳过，否则为活动相机复制遮蔽配置，为非活动相机移除该配置。 参数范围：主世界；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::prepass::specialize_prepass_material_meshes：为变化的可见网格组合采样、预通道、光照贴图、距离渐变及前帧蒙皮形变键，选择深度专用或材质绘制函数并缓存结果；清理禁用预通道、混合透明或读取透射纹理的旧专用化。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_render::view::composition::resolve_composition_spaces：按主纹理及相机顺序汇总空间请求并写回 ResolvedCompositingSpace；全部请求线性时直接归一化，冲突堆栈、非二维相机或 Oklab 缺少有符号存储时回退并警告，共享目标空间不一致时提示混合问题。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_sprite_render::mesh2d::mesh::check_views_need_specialization：根据采样数、目标格式、合成空间及 SDR 相机的着色器内色调映射和抖动设置生成视图键；与缓存不同时更新 ViewKeyCache，并将该视图加入 DirtySpecializations。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_render::view::prepare_view_targets：按相机目标、格式、用途及 MSAA 复用主颜色 A/B 纹理，将清除色转换到实际合成空间并关联输出附件；共享主纹理跨帧复用原子切换状态，无有效尺寸或无需输出的清除相机移除 ViewTarget。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_gizmos_render::pipeline_2d::queue_line_and_joint_gizmos_2d：按视图采样数、目标格式、渲染层及线条样式选择管线，把有效线段列表、线条带和接头加入二维透明阶段；无 GPU 网格、层不相交或顶点不足的部分跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_sprite_render::render::queue_sprites：按相机可见性筛选已提取精灵，结合目标格式、MSAA、色调映射和合成空间选择精灵管线，并将绘制项加入对应透明二维阶段。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::atmosphere::resources::queue_render_sky_pipelines：为具有大气的相机使用 MSAA 样本数和设备双源混合支持构造天空专用化键，取得或排队创建管线并插入 RenderSkyPipelineId。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_core_pipeline::core_2d::prepare_core_2d_depth_textures：在二维主阶段和物理目标尺寸有效时，按渲染目标复用深度纹理，使用相机 MSAA 采样数和二维深度格式，为视图插入深度附件。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_core_pipeline::core_3d::prepare_core_3d_depth_textures：合并同一相机目标所需的深度纹理用途，深度预通道额外要求 COPY_SRC；按目标及 MSAA 采样数复用纹理，并为各视图保存相机指定的深度清除或加载方式。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_core_pipeline::core_3d::prepare_prepass_textures：依据视图标记取得深度、法线、运动矢量、延迟 G-buffer 与光照通道标识纹理，按目标复用并按帧轮换双缓冲；运动矢量存储绑定受设备能力及单采样限制，无预通道阶段时移除旧纹理。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::render::mesh_view_bindings::prepare_mesh_view_bind_groups：按采样与预通道配置选择布局，将视图、光照、聚簇、阴影、探针、雾及透射和大气等资源组成主绑定与纹理数组绑定，保存动态偏移；缺省图像用于适当的替代纹理槽。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::atmosphere::resources::prepare_atmosphere_bind_groups：为大气三维视图建立四类查找表及天空绑定组，关联大气设置、散射介质、光照、坐标变换、查找纹理和视图深度；必需 Uniform 或介质缺失时返回错误，没有深度视图的对象跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_core_pipeline::skybox::prepare_skybox_pipelines：为带 Skybox 的渲染相机，以颜色目标格式、MSAA 采样数及三维深度格式专用化天空盒管线，将缓存标识附到相机。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_post_process::msaa_writeback::prepare_msaa_writeback_pipelines：按主纹理识别首个写入相机，结合 MSAA 回写开关、清除方式及是否后续全屏合成决定是否回写；需要时创建对应采样数和格式的 Blit 管线，否则移除旧回写组件。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_post_process::motion_blur::pipeline::prepare_motion_blur_pipelines：为带 MotionBlurUniform 的已提取相机，依据视图目标格式和 MSAA 采样数专用化运动模糊管线，将缓存标识附到相机。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_post_process::dof::prepare_depth_of_field_view_bind_group_layouts：按 MSAA 选择普通或多采样深度输入，并绑定视图参数和当前颜色；Bokeh 模式额外创建包含辅助颜色纹理的双输入布局，将两种布局附到视图。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_post_process::dof::prepare_depth_of_field_pipelines：结合视图绑定布局、全局布局、目标格式及 MSAA 状态，为 Gaussian 创建水平与垂直管线，为 Bokeh 创建第一和第二通道管线，将缓存标识写入视图。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。

bevy_core_pipeline::prepass::background_motion_vectors::prepare_background_motion_vectors_pipelines：对允许背景运动矢量的预通道视图，依据 MSAA 采样数及法线预通道开关专用化 BackgroundMotionVectorsPipeline，并保存逐视图缓存标识。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::prepass::check_prepass_views_need_specialization：将 MSAA、深度、法线及运动矢量预通道设置组合为视图键；首次出现或键发生变化时更新 ViewKeyPrepassCache，并把视图加入 DirtySpecializations。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::render::mesh::check_views_need_specialization：将格式、采样、预通道、投影、时间抖动、探针和反射、雾、大气、透射等设置组合为网格视图键，新建或变化时标记待专用化，并移除不再出现视图的缓存。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。

schedule-access-e3b40d7b1f14e24a.name: DeferredPrepass
schedule-access-e3b40d7b1f14e24a.description: 使三维相机的延迟材质写入 G-buffer 纹理，供后续延迟光照使用；默认延迟光照还依赖 DepthPrepass。
schedule-access-e3b40d7b1f14e24a.display_summary: 为三维相机启用延迟材质 G-buffer 预通道。
fields:
源码文档：If added to a [`bevy_camera::Camera3d`] then deferred materials will be rendered to the deferred gbuffer texture and will be available to subsequent passes.
Note the default deferred lighting plugin also requires `DepthPrepass` to work correctly.
已核实使用场景：bevy_core_pipeline::core_3d::check_msaa：检查带 DeferredPrepass 的相机，发现启用 MSAA 时发出警告并改为 Msaa::Off，避免延迟渲染使用不兼容的多重采样。 参数范围：main；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::deferred::insert_deferred_lighting_pass_id_component：为启用了 DeferredPrepass 且尚无通道深度标识的视图插入默认 PbrDeferredLightingDepthId，供后续延迟光照通道筛选使用。 参数范围：main；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：bevy_core_pipeline::core_3d::extract_camera_prepass_phase：为活动 Camera3d 按深度、法线、运动矢量及延迟预通道配置创建或移除对应阶段，同步双缓冲标记并根据间接绘制能力选择 GPU 预处理模式，清理本轮失效视图。 参数范围：主世界；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::prepass::specialize_prepass_material_meshes：为变化的可见网格组合采样、预通道、光照贴图、距离渐变及前帧蒙皮形变键，选择深度专用或材质绘制函数并缓存结果；清理禁用预通道、混合透明或读取透射纹理的旧专用化。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
已核实使用场景：bevy_core_pipeline::core_3d::prepare_prepass_textures：依据视图标记取得深度、法线、运动矢量、延迟 G-buffer 与光照通道标识纹理，按目标复用并按帧轮换双缓冲；运动矢量存储绑定受设备能力及单采样限制，无预通道阶段时移除旧纹理。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：bevy_core_pipeline::deferred::copy_lighting_id::prepare_deferred_lighting_id_textures：按启用 DeferredPrepass 的相机物理目标尺寸从纹理缓存取得单采样标识深度纹理，设置渲染附件与复制来源用途并附到视图；无目标尺寸时跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::ssr::prepare_ssr_pipelines：读取视图键与目标格式，专用化屏幕空间反射管线并保存其标识；没有视图键的对象本次跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::deferred::prepare_deferred_lighting_pipelines：从 ViewKeyCache 取得视图键，专用化延迟光照管线并插入标识；没有延迟预通道或带 SkipDeferredLighting 时移除旧管线，缺少视图键时等待后续准备。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::render::mesh::check_views_need_specialization：将格式、采样、预通道、投影、时间抖动、探针和反射、雾、大气、透射等设置组合为网格视图键，新建或变化时标记待专用化，并移除不再出现视图的缓存。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。

源码文档：New-type for [`HashSet`](hb::HashSet) with [`FixedHasher`] as the default hashing provider.
Can be trivially converted to and from a [hashbrown] [`HashSet`](hb::HashSet) using [`From`].

A new-type is used instead of a type alias due to critical methods like [`new`](hb::HashSet::new)
being incompatible with Bevy's choice of default hasher.

Unlike [`hashbrown::HashSet`], [`HashSet`] defaults to [`FixedHasher`]
instead of [`RandomState`](crate::hash::RandomState).
This provides determinism by default with an acceptable compromise to denial
of service resistance in the context of a game engine.

源码文档：A span of text in a tree of spans.

A `TextSpan` is only valid when it exists as a child of a parent that has either `Text` or
`Text2d`. The parent's `Text` / `Text2d` component contains the base text content. Any children
with `TextSpan` extend this text by appending their content to the parent's text in sequence to
form a [`ComputedTextBlock`]. The parent's [`TextLayout`] determines the layout of the block
but each node has its own [`TextFont`] and [`TextColor`].

fields:
源码文档：Headless tab-strip behavior and policy.

Selection is stored separately in [`SelectedTab`]. User interaction emits
[`crate::ValueChange<Option<Entity>>`] from this entity and does not update that state unless
[`tablist_self_update`] is attached as an observer. Activating the already-selected tab does
not re-emit.

Only primary-button clicks change selection. [`InteractionDisabled`] on this entity disables
the whole strip; disabled strips and disabled tabs let pointer and keyboard events propagate
instead of consuming them.
已核实使用场景：bevy_ui_widgets::tabs::update_tablist_derived_state：验证 SelectedTab 必须指向启用的直接子标签，再同步 Selected 标记；按当前焦点、有效选择和第一个可用项的优先级选择唯一 TabIndex(0)，其余标签为 -1，实现标签栏的游走焦点导航。 参数范围：main；存在或变化过滤。

schedule-access-fafd2702bc563ae1.description: 用于禁用态及无障碍状态同步，阻止控件响应操作，但不停止更新或绘制，也不必取消其键盘焦点。
schedule-access-fafd2702bc563ae1.display_summary: 标记禁止交互的 UI 控件。
fields:
源码文档：A component indicating that a widget is disabled and should be "grayed out".
This is used to prevent user interaction with the widget. It should not, however, prevent
the widget from being updated or rendered, or from acquiring keyboard focus.

For apps which support a11y: if a widget (such as a slider) contains multiple entities,
the `InteractionDisabled` component should be added to the root entity of the widget - the
same entity that contains the `AccessibilityNode` component. This will ensure that
the a11y tree is updated correctly.

For developers familiar with the web and HTML, the word "disabled" as used here should be
interpreted as working more like the `aria-disabled` (which doesn't prevent input focus)
than the `disabled` attribute (which does). However, unlike `aria-disabled`, which is purely
advisory, this does make the widget non-operable.

In particular, this marker currently has no effect on the "click-to-focus" observer which
lives in [`bevy_input_focus`], as that is a lower-level crate that this one depends on.

schedule-access-5c75a541e8a19f9b.description: 保存最近两次轮换期间产生的指定类型消息。各 MessageReader 独立维护读取进度，消息写入和读取顺序由调度决定。 本实例类型参数为 bevy_input::gamepad::GamepadConnectionEvent。 消息载荷为 bevy_input::gamepad::GamepadConnectionEvent。
fields:
源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

[`MessageWriter`]: super::MessageWriter

fields:
源码文档：A "press-able" input of type `T`.

## Usage

This type can be used as a resource to keep the current state of an input, by reacting to
events from the input. For a given input value:

* [`ButtonInput::pressed`] will return `true` between a press and a release event.
* [`ButtonInput::just_pressed`] will return `true` for one frame after a press event.
* [`ButtonInput::just_released`] will return `true` for one frame after a release event.

## Multiple systems

In case multiple systems are checking for [`ButtonInput::just_pressed`] or [`ButtonInput::just_released`]
but only one should react, for example when modifying a
[`Resource`], you should consider clearing the input state, either by:

* Using [`ButtonInput::clear_just_pressed`] or [`ButtonInput::clear_just_released`] instead.
* Calling [`ButtonInput::clear`] or [`ButtonInput::reset`] immediately after the state change.

## Performance

For all operations, the following conventions are used:
- **n** is the number of stored inputs.
- **m** is the number of input arguments passed to the method.
- **\***-suffix denotes an amortized cost.
- **~**-suffix denotes an expected cost.

See Rust's [std::collections doc on performance](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/collections/index.html#performance) for more details on the conventions used here.

| **[`ButtonInput`] operations**          | **Computational complexity** |
|-----------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| [`ButtonInput::any_just_pressed`]       | *O*(m)~                      |
| [`ButtonInput::any_just_released`]      | *O*(m)~                      |
| [`ButtonInput::any_pressed`]            | *O*(m)~                      |
| [`ButtonInput::get_just_pressed`]       | *O*(n)                       |
| [`ButtonInput::get_just_released`]      | *O*(n)                       |
| [`ButtonInput::get_pressed`]            | *O*(n)                       |
| [`ButtonInput::just_pressed`]           | *O*(1)~                      |
| [`ButtonInput::just_released`]          | *O*(1)~                      |
| [`ButtonInput::pressed`]                | *O*(1)~                      |
| [`ButtonInput::press`]                  | *O*(1)~*                     |
| [`ButtonInput::release`]                | *O*(1)~*                     |
| [`ButtonInput::release_all`]            | *O*(n)~*                     |
| [`ButtonInput::clear_just_pressed`]     | *O*(1)~                      |
| [`ButtonInput::clear_just_released`]    | *O*(1)~                      |
| [`ButtonInput::reset_all`]              | *O*(n)                       |
| [`ButtonInput::clear`]                  | *O*(n)                       |

## Window focus

`ButtonInput<KeyCode>` is tied to window focus. For example, if the user holds a button
while the window loses focus, [`ButtonInput::just_released`] will be triggered. Similarly if the window
regains focus, [`ButtonInput::just_pressed`] will be triggered.

`ButtonInput<GamepadButton>` is independent of window focus.

## Examples

Reading and checking against the current set of pressed buttons:
```no_run
# use bevy_app::{App, NoopPluginGroup as DefaultPlugins, Update};
# use bevy_ecs::{prelude::{IntoScheduleConfigs, Res, Resource, resource_changed}, schedule::SystemCondition};
# use bevy_input::{ButtonInput, prelude::{KeyCode, MouseButton}};

fn main() {
    App::new()
        .add_plugins(DefaultPlugins)
        .add_systems(
            Update,
            print_mouse.run_if(resource_changed::<ButtonInput<MouseButton>>),
        )
        .add_systems(
            Update,
            print_keyboard.run_if(resource_changed::<ButtonInput<KeyCode>>),
        )
        .run();
}

fn print_mouse(mouse: Res<ButtonInput<MouseButton>>) {
    println!("Mouse: {:?}", mouse.get_pressed().collect::<Vec<_>>());
}

fn print_keyboard(keyboard: Res<ButtonInput<KeyCode>>) {
    if keyboard.any_pressed([KeyCode::ControlLeft, KeyCode::ControlRight])
        && keyboard.any_pressed([KeyCode::AltLeft, KeyCode::AltRight])
        && keyboard.any_pressed([KeyCode::ShiftLeft, KeyCode::ShiftRight])
        && keyboard.any_pressed([KeyCode::SuperLeft, KeyCode::SuperRight])
        && keyboard.pressed(KeyCode::KeyL)
    {
        println!("On Windows this opens LinkedIn.");
    } else {
        println!("keyboard: {:?}", keyboard.get_pressed().collect::<Vec<_>>());
    }
}
```

## Note

When adding this resource for a new input type, you should:

* Call the [`ButtonInput::press`] method for each press event.
* Call the [`ButtonInput::release`] method for each release event.
* Call the [`ButtonInput::clear`] method at each frame start, before processing events.

Note: Calling `clear` from a [`ResMut`] will trigger change detection.
It may be preferable to use [`DetectChangesMut::bypass_change_detection`]
to avoid causing the resource to always be marked as changed.

Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
```

with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages

    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
```

源码文档：A collection of [`Touch`]es.

## Usage

It is used to create a `bevy` resource that stores the data of the touches on a touchscreen
and can be accessed inside of a system.

schedule-access-ae0cbfe890d126ab.name: Messages<PointerHits>
schedule-access-ae0cbfe890d126ab.description: 保存最近两次轮换期间产生的指定类型消息。各 MessageReader 独立维护读取进度，消息写入和读取顺序由调度决定。 本实例类型参数为 bevy_picking::backend::PointerHits。 消息载荷为 bevy_picking::backend::PointerHits。
fields:
源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

[`MessageReader`]: super::MessageReader
[`MessageWriter`]: super::MessageWriter
[`message_update_system`]: super::message_update_system

schedule-access-2c07cb4712b5504c.name: Messages<Ime>
schedule-access-2c07cb4712b5504c.description: 保存最近两次轮换期间产生的指定类型消息。各 MessageReader 独立维护读取进度，消息写入和读取顺序由调度决定。 本实例类型参数为 bevy_window::event::Ime。 消息载荷为 bevy_window::event::Ime。
fields:
源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

[`MessageWriter`]: super::MessageWriter
[`message_update_system`]: super::message_update_system

schedule-access-50e09411dac64872.name: PointerCaptureMap
schedule-access-50e09411dac64872.description: 保存指针捕获目标，用单个实体覆盖普通悬停命中，使拖动离开边界后仍持续交互；释放或取消时解除。
fields:
源码文档：Overrides the [`HoverMap`] for captured pointers, forcing a single entity to be reported as
hovered regardless of where the pointer physically is.

When a pointer is captured by an entity, that entity is reported as the sole hover target for
that pointer. This keeps interactions (like dragging a slider) working correctly even when the
pointer drifts outside the entity's bounding box while a button is held.

Use [`PointerCaptureMap::capture`] to lock a pointer to an entity, and
[`PointerCaptureMap::release`] to remove the lock. Captures are automatically cleaned up when
the associated pointer entity is removed.

A pointer's capture is also released automatically when that pointer reports a button release
or cancel action.

源码文档：A component that aggregates picking interaction state of this entity across all pointers.

Unlike bevy's `Interaction` component, this is an aggregate of the state of all pointers
interacting with this entity. Aggregation is done by taking the interaction with the highest
precedence.

the entity will be considered pressed. If that entity is instead being hovered by both pointers,
it will be considered hovered.

源码文档：A component that allows users to use regular Bevy change detection to determine when the pointer
enters or leaves an entity. Users should insert this component on an entity to indicate interest
in knowing about hover state changes.

The component's boolean value will be `true` whenever the pointer is currently directly hovering
over the entity, or any of the entity's descendants (as defined by the [`ChildOf`]
relationship). This is consistent with the behavior of the CSS `:hover` pseudo-class, which
applies to the element and all of its descendants.

The contained boolean value is guaranteed to only be mutated when the pointer enters or leaves
the entity, allowing Bevy change detection to be used efficiently. This is in contrast to the
[`HoverMap`] resource, which is updated every frame.

Typically, a simple hoverable entity or widget will have this component added to it. More
complex widgets can have this component added to each hoverable part.

The computational cost of keeping the `Hovered` components up to date is relatively cheap, and
linear in the number of entities that have the [`Hovered`] component inserted.

源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

[`MessageWriter`]: super::MessageWriter
[`message_update_system`]: super::message_update_system

fields:
源码文档：Fires when a pointer crosses out of the bounds of a [target entity](EntityEvent::event_target).
Unlike [`PointerOut`], this event bubbles up through a subset of the
[target entity's](EntityEvent::event_target) ancestors
(traversed via the [`ChildOf`] relationship).

### Event Propagation
An ancestor of a [target entity](EntityEvent::event_target) will receive a [`PointerLeave`] event
when the ancestor does not have a direct relation to any entity hovered by the
pointer in the current frame. For example, for a given pointer:

If the previously hovered entity C has the following entity ancestry: A -> B -> C

And the currently hovered entity E has the following entity ancestry: A -> D -> E

[`PointerLeave`] events would be sent for both C and its direct ancestor B.
A [`PointerLeave`] event would not be sent for A because it is a shared ancestor of both C and E.

Note: A [`PointerLeave`] event may be fired for an ancestor even if the pointer does not leave
the ancestor's bounds. More concretely, if a child's bounds extend beyond the parent's
and the pointer leaves from within those extended bounds,
two [`PointerLeave`] events are still emitted for both the child and the parent.
This matches the triggering behavior of `mouseleave` events on the web.
To find out whether the pointer was within the target entity's bounds
right before leaving, check the value of [`was_in_bounds`](PointerLeave::was_in_bounds).

Refer to [`pointer_events`] for more information on how these events are triggered.

schedule-access-008dd1791e924313.name: PointerEnter
schedule-access-008dd1791e924313.description: 指针进入目标时触发，携带命中及is_in_bounds；只传播到上帧没有悬停子孙的祖先，已被前后悬停实体共同覆盖的祖先不再收到进入事件。
schedule-access-008dd1791e924313.display_summary: 通知指针进入目标或其独有祖先范围。
fields:
源码文档：Fires when a pointer crosses into the bounds of a [target entity](EntityEvent::event_target).
Unlike [`PointerOver`], this event bubbles up through a subset of the
[target entity's](EntityEvent::event_target) ancestors
(traversed via the [`ChildOf`] relationship).

### Event Propagation
An ancestor of a [target entity](EntityEvent::event_target) will receive an [`PointerEnter`] event
when the ancestor does not have a direct relation to any entity hovered by the
pointer in the previous frame. For example, for a given pointer:

If the previously hovered entity C has the following entity ancestry: A -> B -> C

And the currently hovered entity E has the following entity ancestry: A -> D -> E

[`PointerEnter`] events would be sent for both E and its direct ancestor D.
An [`PointerEnter`] event would not be sent for A because it is a shared ancestor of both C and E.

Note: An [`PointerEnter`] event may be fired for an ancestor even if the pointer does not enter
within the ancestor's bounds. More concretely, if a child's bounds extend beyond the parent's
and the pointer enters the child's bounds without crossing into the parent's,
two [`PointerEnter`] events are still emitted for both the child and the parent.
This matches the triggering behavior of `mouseenter` events on the web.
To find out whether a pointer is within the target entity's bounds
immediately upon entering, check the value of [`is_in_bounds`](PointerEnter::is_in_bounds).

Refer to [`pointer_events`] for more information on how these events are triggered.

源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

源码文档：A "press-able" input of type `T`.

## Usage

This type can be used as a resource to keep the current state of an input, by reacting to
events from the input. For a given input value:

* [`ButtonInput::pressed`] will return `true` between a press and a release event.
* [`ButtonInput::just_pressed`] will return `true` for one frame after a press event.
* [`ButtonInput::just_released`] will return `true` for one frame after a release event.

## Multiple systems

In case multiple systems are checking for [`ButtonInput::just_pressed`] or [`ButtonInput::just_released`]
but only one should react, for example when modifying a
[`Resource`], you should consider clearing the input state, either by:

* Using [`ButtonInput::clear_just_pressed`] or [`ButtonInput::clear_just_released`] instead.
* Calling [`ButtonInput::clear`] or [`ButtonInput::reset`] immediately after the state change.

## Performance

For all operations, the following conventions are used:
- **n** is the number of stored inputs.
- **m** is the number of input arguments passed to the method.
- **\***-suffix denotes an amortized cost.
- **~**-suffix denotes an expected cost.

See Rust's [std::collections doc on performance](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/collections/index.html#performance) for more details on the conventions used here.

| **[`ButtonInput`] operations**          | **Computational complexity** |
|-----------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| [`ButtonInput::any_just_pressed`]       | *O*(m)~                      |
| [`ButtonInput::any_just_released`]      | *O*(m)~                      |
| [`ButtonInput::any_pressed`]            | *O*(m)~                      |
| [`ButtonInput::get_just_pressed`]       | *O*(n)                       |
| [`ButtonInput::get_just_released`]      | *O*(n)                       |
| [`ButtonInput::get_pressed`]            | *O*(n)                       |
| [`ButtonInput::just_pressed`]           | *O*(1)~                      |
| [`ButtonInput::just_released`]          | *O*(1)~                      |
| [`ButtonInput::pressed`]                | *O*(1)~                      |
| [`ButtonInput::press`]                  | *O*(1)~*                     |
| [`ButtonInput::release`]                | *O*(1)~*                     |
| [`ButtonInput::release_all`]            | *O*(n)~*                     |
| [`ButtonInput::clear_just_pressed`]     | *O*(1)~                      |
| [`ButtonInput::clear_just_released`]    | *O*(1)~                      |
| [`ButtonInput::reset_all`]              | *O*(n)                       |
| [`ButtonInput::clear`]                  | *O*(n)                       |

## Window focus

`ButtonInput<KeyCode>` is tied to window focus. For example, if the user holds a button
while the window loses focus, [`ButtonInput::just_released`] will be triggered. Similarly if the window
regains focus, [`ButtonInput::just_pressed`] will be triggered.

`ButtonInput<GamepadButton>` is independent of window focus.

## Examples

Reading and checking against the current set of pressed buttons:
```no_run
# use bevy_app::{App, NoopPluginGroup as DefaultPlugins, Update};
# use bevy_ecs::{prelude::{IntoScheduleConfigs, Res, Resource, resource_changed}, schedule::SystemCondition};
# use bevy_input::{ButtonInput, prelude::{KeyCode, MouseButton}};

fn main() {
    App::new()
        .add_plugins(DefaultPlugins)
        .add_systems(
            Update,
            print_mouse.run_if(resource_changed::<ButtonInput<MouseButton>>),
        )
        .add_systems(
            Update,
            print_keyboard.run_if(resource_changed::<ButtonInput<KeyCode>>),
        )
        .run();
}

fn print_mouse(mouse: Res<ButtonInput<MouseButton>>) {
    println!("Mouse: {:?}", mouse.get_pressed().collect::<Vec<_>>());
}

fn print_keyboard(keyboard: Res<ButtonInput<KeyCode>>) {
    if keyboard.any_pressed([KeyCode::ControlLeft, KeyCode::ControlRight])
        && keyboard.any_pressed([KeyCode::AltLeft, KeyCode::AltRight])
        && keyboard.any_pressed([KeyCode::ShiftLeft, KeyCode::ShiftRight])
        && keyboard.any_pressed([KeyCode::SuperLeft, KeyCode::SuperRight])
        && keyboard.pressed(KeyCode::KeyL)
    {
        println!("On Windows this opens LinkedIn.");
    } else {
        println!("keyboard: {:?}", keyboard.get_pressed().collect::<Vec<_>>());
    }
}
```

## Note

When adding this resource for a new input type, you should:

* Call the [`ButtonInput::press`] method for each press event.
* Call the [`ButtonInput::release`] method for each release event.
* Call the [`ButtonInput::clear`] method at each frame start, before processing events.

Note: Calling `clear` from a [`ResMut`] will trigger change detection.
It may be preferable to use [`DetectChangesMut::bypass_change_detection`]
to avoid causing the resource to always be marked as changed.

fields:
源码文档：Bitset with events caused by state transitions of [`TriggerState`].
/// During [`EnhancedInputSystems::Trigger`], events that correspond to bitflags will be triggered.
/// You can use this component directly in systems or react on corresponding events in observers.
/// Table of state transitions:
/// | Last state                  | New state                | Events                    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| [`TriggerState::None`]       | [`TriggerState::None`]    | No events                 |
| [`TriggerState::None`]       | [`TriggerState::Ongoing`] | [`Start`] + [`Ongoing`] |
| [`TriggerState::None`]       | [`TriggerState::Fired`]   | [`Start`] + [`Fire`]   |
| [`TriggerState::Ongoing`]    | [`TriggerState::None`]    | [`Cancel`]              |
| [`TriggerState::Ongoing`]    | [`TriggerState::Ongoing`] | [`Ongoing`]               |
| [`TriggerState::Ongoing`]    | [`TriggerState::Fired`]   | [`Fire`]                 |
| [`TriggerState::Fired`]      | [`TriggerState::Fired`]   | [`Fire`]                 |
| [`TriggerState::Fired`]      | [`TriggerState::Ongoing`] | [`Ongoing`]               |
| [`TriggerState::Fired`]      | [`TriggerState::None`]    | [`Complete`]             |
/// The meaning of each kind depends on the assigned [`InputCondition`]s. The events are

schedule-access-09e74a46727f1554.name: Messages<UntypedAssetLoadFailedEvent>
schedule-access-09e74a46727f1554.description: 保存最近两次轮换期间产生的指定类型消息。各 MessageReader 独立维护读取进度，消息写入和读取顺序由调度决定。 本实例类型参数为 bevy_asset::event::UntypedAssetLoadFailedEvent。 消息载荷为 bevy_asset::event::UntypedAssetLoadFailedEvent。
fields:
源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

[`MessageReader`]: super::MessageReader
[`MessageWriter`]: super::MessageWriter
[`message_update_system`]: super::message_update_system
本实例类型参数：bevy_asset::event::UntypedAssetLoadFailedEvent

fields:
源码文档：A 3D camera component. Enables the main 3D render graph for a [`Camera`].

The camera coordinate space is right-handed X-right, Y-up, Z-back.
This means "forward" is -Z.
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::prepass::update_mesh_previous_global_transforms：有活动视图时，为缺少历史变换的网格插入初值，仅在当前 GlobalTransform 更新较晚时同步已有 PreviousGlobalTransform，供后续运动相关计算使用。 参数范围：main；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::prepass::update_previous_view_data：根据主世界相机投影与世界变换计算视图、裁剪及逆矩阵，保存为 PreviousViewData；渲染侧的时间抖动随后另行补入。 参数范围：main；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：bevy_ui_render::extract_ui_camera_view：以左上角为原点建立视口正交投影，复用或创建 UI 子视图和透明阶段，双向关联主相机并复制抗锯齿及阴影采样设置；相机无效、停用或移除后销毁关联视图并清理阶段，兼容同帧移除重加。 参数范围：主世界；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：bevy_core_pipeline::core_3d::extract_core_3d_camera_phases：为每个活动 Camera3d 建立不透明、AlphaMask 和透明三维阶段，按平台支持及间接绘制开关设置 GPU 预处理模式，并移除失效视图的阶段。 参数范围：主世界；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：bevy_core_pipeline::core_3d::extract_camera_prepass_phase：为活动 Camera3d 按深度、法线、运动矢量及延迟预通道配置创建或移除对应阶段，同步双缓冲标记并根据间接绘制能力选择 GPU 预处理模式，清理本轮失效视图。 参数范围：主世界；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::prepass::extract_camera_previous_view_data：对活动三维相机复制已存在的 PreviousViewData 到对应渲染实体；相机停用时移除旧前帧视图组件。 参数范围：主世界；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::light_probe::gather_light_probes<bevy_light::probe::EnvironmentMapLight>：逐视图筛选可见集合中指定类型的探针，跳过图像未加载的候选并按相机距离排序，构建该视图的探针与纹理映射；结果为空时移除旧探针组件。 参数范围：主世界；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::light_probe::gather_light_probes<bevy_light::probe::IrradianceVolume>：逐视图筛选可见集合中指定类型的探针，跳过图像未加载的候选并按相机距离排序，构建该视图的探针与纹理映射；结果为空时移除旧探针组件。 参数范围：主世界；存在或变化过滤。
已核实使用场景：bevy_pbr::transmission::phase::extract_transmissive_camera_phases：从主世界读取相机，为活动 Camera3d 的主子视图准备新的透射排序阶段，记录存活视图集合，最后移除本帧未出现的透射阶段。 参数范围：主世界；存在或变化过滤。

源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)

schedule-access-30744da00cc8e67f.name: FocusedNonWindowEguiContext
schedule-access-30744da00cc8e67f.description: 保存当前获得键盘焦点的非窗口 Egui 上下文实体。指针按下或触摸开始时根据悬停目标更新。
schedule-access-30744da00cc8e67f.display_summary: 保存当前获得键盘焦点的非窗口 Egui 上下文实体
fields:
源码文档：Stores an entity of a focused non-window context (to push keyboard messages to).

The resource won't exist if no context is focused, [`Option<Res<FocusedNonWindowEguiContext>>`] must be used to read from it.
If the [`HoveredNonWindowEguiContext`] resource exists, the [`FocusedNonWindowEguiContext`]
resource will get inserted on mouse button press or touch start message
(and removed if no hovered non-window context exists respectively).

Atm, it's up to users to update [`HoveredNonWindowEguiContext`] and [`EguiContextPointerPosition`].
We might be able to add proper `bevy_picking` support for world space UI once [`bevy_picking::backend::HitData`]
starts exposing triangle index or UV.

Updating focused contexts happens during [`crate::EguiInputSet::FocusContext`],
see [`write_pointer_moved_and_button_messages_system`] and [`write_window_touch_messages_system`].

schedule-access-9cc29522ef3393a7.display_summary: 把输入消息与对应的 Egui 上下文配对迭代
fields: 源码文档：A helper system param to iterate over pairs of messages and Egui contexts, see [`EguiContextsMessageIterator`].

schedule-access-3dc4a7192b717a5f.description: 保存最近两次轮换期间产生的指定类型消息。各 MessageReader 独立维护读取进度，消息写入和读取顺序由调度决定。 本实例类型参数为 bevy_window::event::CursorMoved。 消息载荷为 bevy_window::event::CursorMoved。
fields:
源码文档：A message collection that represents the messages that occurred within the last two
[`Messages::update`] calls.
Messages can be written to using a [`MessageWriter`]
and are typically cheaply read using a [`MessageReader`].

Each message can be consumed by multiple systems, in parallel,
with consumption tracked by the [`MessageReader`] on a per-system basis.

If no [ordering](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/examples/ecs/ecs_guide.rs)
is applied between writing and reading systems, there is a risk of a race condition.
This means that whether the messages arrive before or after the next [`Messages::update`] is unpredictable.

This collection is meant to be paired with a system that calls
[`Messages::update`] exactly once per update/frame.

[`message_update_system`] is a system that does this, typically initialized automatically using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).
[`MessageReader`]s are expected to read messages from this collection at least once per loop/frame.
Messages will persist across a single frame boundary and so ordering of message producers and
consumers is not critical (although poorly-planned ordering may cause accumulating lag).
If messages are not handled by the end of the frame after they are updated, they will be
dropped silently.

# Example

```
use bevy_ecs::message::{Message, Messages};

#[derive(Message)]
struct MyMessage {
    value: usize
}

// setup
let mut messages = Messages::<MyMessage>::default();
let mut cursor = messages.get_cursor();

// run this once per update/frame
messages.update();

// somewhere else: write a message
messages.write(MyMessage { value: 1 });

// somewhere else: read the messages
for message in cursor.read(&messages) {
    assert_eq!(message.value, 1)
}

// messages are only processed once per reader
assert_eq!(cursor.read(&messages).count(), 0);
```

# Details

[`Messages`] is implemented using a variation of a double buffer strategy.
Each call to [`update`](Messages::update) swaps buffers and clears out the oldest one.
- [`MessageReader`]s will read messages from both buffers.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read at least once per update will never drop messages.
- [`MessageReader`]s that read once within two updates might still receive some messages
- [`MessageReader`]s that read after two updates are guaranteed to drop all messages that occurred
  before those updates.

The buffers in [`Messages`] will grow indefinitely if [`update`](Messages::update) is never called.

An alternative call pattern would be to call [`update`](Messages::update)
manually across frames to control when messages are cleared.
This complicates consumption and risks ever-expanding memory usage if not cleaned up,
but can be done by adding your message as a resource instead of using
[`add_message`](https://docs.rs/bevy/*/bevy/app/struct.App.html#method.add_message).

[Example usage.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/examples/ecs/message.rs)
[Example usage standalone.](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/latest/crates/bevy_ecs/examples/messages.rs)

[`MessageWriter`]: super::MessageWriter
[`message_update_system`]: super::message_update_system

bevy_pbr::render::gpu_preprocess::early_gpu_preprocess：根据直接绘制、GPU 视锥或早期遮挡裁剪选择计算管线，遍历各视图的绘制阶段，对索引及非索引工作项调度网格预处理；资源或管线未就绪的阶段跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::render::gpu_preprocess::early_prepass_build_indirect_parameters：对当前视图调用共享参数构建流程，使用 early_phase 管线和批次元数据，为绘制上一帧已可见对象的早期预通道准备间接命令。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::render::gpu_preprocess::late_gpu_preprocess：在启用遮挡裁剪及深度预通道、且未禁用间接绘制的视图上，使用后期管线和索引、非索引间接工作量执行转换与裁剪；管线未就绪时返回。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::render::gpu_preprocess::late_prepass_build_indirect_parameters：对当前视图调用共享参数构建流程，选用 late_phase 管线，为遮挡裁剪后新出现、上一帧不可见的对象准备多重间接绘制命令。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::render::gpu_preprocess::main_build_indirect_parameters：对非阴影视图调用共享参数构建流程，使用 main_phase 管线和视图批次元数据，生成主绘制阶段所需的多重间接命令。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_render::camera::expire_specializations_for_views：收集当前 ExtractedView 的 RetainedViewEntity，仅在 DirtySpecializations.views 中保留仍存在的视图身份。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_render::camera::expire_wireframe_specializations_for_views：依据当前已提取视图的稳定身份，过滤 DirtyWireframeSpecializations.views 中不再存在的视图，避免线框专用化处理已删除视图。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::prepass::specialize_prepass_material_meshes：为变化的可见网格组合采样、预通道、光照贴图、距离渐变及前帧蒙皮形变键，选择深度专用或材质绘制函数并缓存结果；清理禁用预通道、混合透明或读取透射纹理的旧专用化。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::render::mesh::collect_gpu_culled_meshes：分别遍历相机和光源阴影子视图，把全局潜在可见 GPU 裁剪实体按各自渲染层交给共享收集逻辑，并传入集合新增状态或变化刻度。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。
bevy_render::view::composition::resolve_composition_spaces：按主纹理及相机顺序汇总空间请求并写回 ResolvedCompositingSpace；全部请求线性时直接归一化，冲突堆栈、非二维相机或 Oklab 缺少有符号存储时回退并警告，共享目标空间不一致时提示混合问题。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_sprite_render::mesh2d::mesh::check_views_need_specialization：根据采样数、目标格式、合成空间及 SDR 相机的着色器内色调映射和抖动设置生成视图键；与缓存不同时更新 ViewKeyCache，并将该视图加入 DirtySpecializations。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::render::light::prepare_lights：汇总提取后的各类光源，为视图准备光照 GPU 参数、聚簇索引及阴影贴图和阴影视图，维护对应缓存及阶段记录，并检查设备和实现支持的数量限制。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_sprite_render::mesh2d::material::prepare_pending_mesh_material2d_queues：为每个已提取视图将当前帧与前帧待处理队列切换到新帧状态，记录活跃视图集合并移除已不存在视图的队列。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_sprite_render::mesh2d::material::specialize_material2d_meshes：按视图和实体脏标记清除旧缓存，组合视图键、网格布局和材质属性收集专用化任务，更新材质绑定索引并生成管线缓存；网格或材质未准备时进入待处理队列，失败记录错误，最后清理失效视图缓存。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::material::specialize_material_meshes：合并视图、几何、材质、光照贴图、可见范围及前帧蒙皮形变特性构造管线键，调用材质专用化回调并按视图保存结果；清理旧缓存及失效视图，实例或材质未就绪时保留重试项。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::render::light::check_views_lights_need_specialization：对具有阴影绘制阶段的光源视图构造深度键，平行光采用正交及不裁剪深度标志，其他光源采用透视标志；新键或变化的键写入缓存并标记视图待专用化。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::render::light::specialize_shadows：按阴影视图、网格及材质变化重新选择专用阴影渲染管线，清理失效缓存，并整理需要补齐或重新排队的阴影网格任务。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_render::view::prepare_view_targets：按相机目标、格式、用途及 MSAA 复用主颜色 A/B 纹理，将清除色转换到实际合成空间并关联输出附件；共享主纹理跨帧复用原子切换状态，无有效尺寸或无需输出的清除相机移除 ViewTarget。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_sprite_render::mesh2d::material::queue_material2d_meshes：先从保留阶段移除不可见或失去网格材质的实体，再处理新可见、脏专用化及待就绪实体；材质未准备时留到后续重试，已就绪时按 Opaque、Mask 或透明模式加入对应阶段，并按网格批处理能力及深度偏移生成批次信息。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::prepass::queue_prepass_material_meshes：移除失效分桶项并重试待办，根据不透明或遮罩材质及前向、延迟方法选择对应阶段，记录管线、绘制函数和网格分块；实例或材质未就绪时保留重试项。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::material::queue_material_meshes：移除失效绘制项，重试新可见或待更新网格，按透射配置和材质模式分配不透明、遮罩、透射或透明阶段；材质或实例未就绪时保留待办，延迟不透明项仅更新缓存。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::render::light::queue_shadows：遍历各阴影视图中可见的网格，按专用材质管线、渲染层及投影资格更新阴影分桶；移除失效项，将资产或管线尚未就绪的网格留到后续重试。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_gizmos_render::pipeline_2d::queue_line_and_joint_gizmos_2d：按视图采样数、目标格式、渲染层及线条样式选择管线，把有效线段列表、线条带和接头加入二维透明阶段；无 GPU 网格、层不相交或顶点不足的部分跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_gizmos_render::pipeline_3d::queue_line_gizmos_3d：对具备视图键的三维阶段，按渲染层、透视线宽与样式专用化管线，将已有 GPU 顶点的线列表和线条带作为置顶项加入透明阶段；管线专用化错误向调用方返回。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_gizmos_render::pipeline_3d::queue_line_joint_gizmos_3d：在视图及 Gizmo 渲染层相交、折线至少三个顶点且启用接头时，按视图键、透视线宽和接头形状选择管线，并把接头绘制作为置顶透明项排队。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_sprite_render::render::queue_sprites：按相机可见性筛选已提取精灵，结合目标格式、MSAA、色调映射和合成空间选择精灵管线，并将绘制项加入对应透明二维阶段。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_ui_render::queue_uinodes：为提取的 UI 节点找到目标相机的透明 UI 阶段，按目标格式与 UI 抗锯齿设置选择管线，并以节点堆叠顺序加入本帧绘制项。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。
bevy_ui_render::queue_uinodes：为提取的 UI 节点找到目标相机的透明 UI 阶段，按目标格式与 UI 抗锯齿设置选择管线，并以节点堆叠顺序加入本帧绘制项。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_ui_render::ui_texture_slice_pipeline::queue_ui_slices：为各切片找到主相机的 UI 子视图和透明阶段，按目标颜色格式专用化切片管线，以节点堆叠顺序加图像偏移生成排序键并加入临时绘制项；缺少相机或阶段时跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。
bevy_ui_render::ui_texture_slice_pipeline::queue_ui_slices：为各切片找到主相机的 UI 子视图和透明阶段，按目标颜色格式专用化切片管线，以节点堆叠顺序加图像偏移生成排序键并加入临时绘制项；缺少相机或阶段时跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_ui_render::gradient::queue_gradient：将提取的背景和边框渐变加入目标相机的透明 UI 阶段，按颜色空间、目标格式及抗锯齿配置选择管线，并保留各自堆叠偏移。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。
bevy_ui_render::gradient::queue_gradient：将提取的背景和边框渐变加入目标相机的透明 UI 阶段，按颜色空间、目标格式及抗锯齿配置选择管线，并保留各自堆叠偏移。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_ui_render::box_shadow::queue_shadows：为提取的 UI 阴影选择匹配目标格式和阴影采样数的管线，按节点堆叠顺序及阴影层偏移加入透明 UI 绘制阶段。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。
bevy_ui_render::box_shadow::queue_shadows：为提取的 UI 阴影选择匹配目标格式和阴影采样数的管线，按节点堆叠顺序及阴影层偏移加入透明 UI 绘制阶段。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_core_pipeline::oit::resolve::queue_oit_resolve_pipeline：以目标格式、最大排序片元数及深度预通道开关生成专用化键，复用未变视图的缓存管线，否则排队新管线并附到相机；清理已消失视图的本地缓存。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_egui::render::systems::queue_pipelines_system：遍历 Egui 视图所指向的相机，根据 HDR 或普通目标格式特化 EguiPipeline，把主实体到缓存管线身份的映射写入 EguiPipelines；缺少相机数据的视图跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。
bevy_render::render_phase::sort_phase_system<bevy_core_pipeline::core_2d::Transparent2d>：对当前已提取视图找到相应 SortedRenderPhase，先按视图重算排序键再执行该阶段类型的排序；缺少阶段的视图跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_render::render_phase::sort_phase_system<bevy_core_pipeline::core_3d::Transparent3d>：对当前已提取视图找到相应 SortedRenderPhase，先按视图重算排序键再执行该阶段类型的排序；缺少阶段的视图跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_render::render_phase::sort_phase_system<bevy_ui_render::render_pass::TransparentUi>：对当前已提取视图找到相应 SortedRenderPhase，先按视图重算排序键再执行该阶段类型的排序；缺少阶段的视图跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_render::render_phase::sort_phase_system<bevy_pbr::transmission::phase::Transmissive3d>：对当前已提取视图找到相应 SortedRenderPhase，先按视图重算排序键再执行该阶段类型的排序；缺少阶段的视图跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_render::view::prepare_view_uniforms：为各视图计算带抖动与无抖动矩阵、逆矩阵、视锥平面、主通道分辨率、曝光和颜色分级，并写入帧号及 mip 偏置；依据相机或阴影视图来源选择 LOD 参考位置，上传后附加逐视图参数偏移。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_core_pipeline::core_2d::prepare_core_2d_depth_textures：在二维主阶段和物理目标尺寸有效时，按渲染目标复用深度纹理，使用相机 MSAA 采样数和二维深度格式，为视图插入深度附件。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_core_pipeline::core_3d::prepare_prepass_textures：依据视图标记取得深度、法线、运动矢量、延迟 G-buffer 与光照通道标识纹理，按目标复用并按帧轮换双缓冲；运动矢量存储绑定受设备能力及单采样限制，无预通道阶段时移除旧纹理。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_anti_alias::smaa::prepare_smaa_uniforms：清空本轮 SMAA 参数集合，写入各视图宽高及倒数，保存每个视图的动态参数偏移，再把统一参数缓冲上传 GPU。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_anti_alias::smaa::prepare_smaa_textures：根据相机物理目标尺寸，从纹理缓存取得 RG 边缘纹理、8 位模板和 RGBA 混合纹理并附到视图；没有目标尺寸的相机跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。
bevy_anti_alias::taa::prepare_taa_history_textures：根据视图目标尺寸和格式取得两张历史颜色纹理，按 FrameCount 奇偶交换 read 与 write，附到启用 TAA 的相机；无物理目标尺寸时跳过。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::prepass::prepare_previous_view_uniforms：取得前帧视图数据，缺失时用当前视图初始化，再重施上一帧实际抖动以匹配旧深度与几何缓冲；上传后保存偏移，并记录本帧抖动及实际主通道尺寸供下帧使用。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::render::fog::prepare_fog：把各提取视图的 DistanceFog 转换为线性、指数、平方指数或大气模式的 GPU 参数，写入雾 Uniform 缓冲，并记录视图所用偏移。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。
bevy_pbr::light_probe::upload_light_probes：将视图环境图的索引、强度、逆旋转和 mip 设置，与数量受上限约束的反射及辐照探针打包到 Uniform 缓冲，为每个视图保存动态偏移。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。
bevy_pbr::ssr::prepare_ssr_settings：按视图数量申请反射 Uniform 写入器，写入每份 ScreenSpaceReflectionsUniform 并在对应实体插入动态索引；无法取得写入器时返回。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。
bevy_pbr::transmission::texture::prepare_core_3d_transmission_textures：仅处理渲染阶段齐备、有物理目标尺寸、透射步数非零且存在透射物体的视图；同一目标复用缓存纹理，创建线性采样器并插入 ViewTransmissionTexture。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::contact_shadows::prepare_contact_shadows_settings：为视图数量取得接触阴影 Uniform 写入器，将每个 ContactShadows 转为 GPU 参数，写入共享缓冲并插入该视图的参数偏移。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。

bevy_render::batching::gpu_preprocessing::delete_old_work_item_buffers<bevy_pbr::render::mesh::MeshPipeline>：在视图提取完成后收集现存 RetainedViewEntity，对每个阶段的 work_item_buffers 仅保留仍存在视图的条目，避免删除视图的工作缓冲持续占用。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
bevy_pbr::atmosphere::resources::prepare_atmosphere_transforms：依据相机在大气空间的位置确定地表法线和正交基，写入动态变换 Uniform，并为视图保存对应偏移；极点退化时改用备用参考方向。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。

bevy_render::batching::gpu_preprocessing::batch_and_prepare_binned_render_phase<bevy_core_pipeline::core_3d::Opaque3d, bevy_pbr::render::mesh::MeshPipeline>：先为不可批与普通批实例分配输出槽、预处理任务及可选间接绘制参数，再为多重间接绘制的分桶生成批集合和参数范围；保留 CPU 初始化任务在 GPU 解包任务之前的顺序，并为遮挡剔除预留晚期任务空间。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。

bevy_render::batching::gpu_preprocessing::batch_and_prepare_binned_render_phase<bevy_core_pipeline::core_3d::Opaque3d, bevy_pbr::render::mesh::MeshPipeline>：先为不可批与普通批实例分配输出槽、预处理任务及可选间接绘制参数，再为多重间接绘制的分桶生成批集合和参数范围；保留 CPU 初始化任务在 GPU 解包任务之前的顺序，并为遮挡剔除预留晚期任务空间。 参数范围：RenderApp；存在或变化过滤。

bevy_render::batching::gpu_preprocessing::batch_and_prepare_binned_render_phase<bevy_core_pipeline::core_3d::AlphaMask3d, bevy_pbr::render::mesh::MeshPipeline>：先为不可批与普通批实例分配输出槽、预处理任务及可选间接绘制参数，再为多重间接绘制的分桶生成批集合和参数范围；保留 CPU 初始化任务在 GPU 解包任务之前的顺序，并为遮挡剔除预留晚期任务空间。 参数范围：RenderApp；只读声明。
